title: Recitals and Background
purpose: Recitals provide factual background and commercial context for the transaction, establishing the parties' understanding of why the Agreement is being entered into and what commercial objectives it is intended to achieve. Well-drafted Recitals assist in contract interpretation if disputes arise, particularly where operative clauses are ambiguous or silent on intent. However, Recitals must not create substantive obligations, representations or warranties that are not reflected in the operative cla
baseline:
Recitals.
(A) [Describe each Party and its business or role relevant to this transaction.]
(B) [Describe the commercial background: why the Parties are entering into this relationship, and the business problem or opportunity being addressed.]
(C) [Describe what each Party will do under this Agreement: the Company will [provide / procure / license], and the Counterparty will [provide / procure / license].]
(D) [State any relevant factual assumptions, regulatory context or prior dealings between the Parties that provide necessary context.]
NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants in this Agreement and for other good and valuable consideration (the receipt and sufficiency of which are acknowledged), the Parties agree as set out below.
redflags:
Recitals contain service commitments, performance standards, guaranteed volumes, delivery timelines, regulatory status claims, product specifications, system capabilities, exclusivity arrangements or customer promises that are not reflected in the operative clauses with enforceable terms, conditions, deadlines and remedies.
Recitals reference prior agreements, understandings, term sheets or negotiations that have not been fully documented or superseded by this Agreement (risk of collateral obligations).
usageNotes: Recitals are drafted jointly by Business. Business provides the factual background, commercial rationale and description of what each Party is doing; Legal reviews to ensure Recitals do not create unintended obligations. Recitals should be concise (typically 3-5 paragraphs), factual (not aspirational or promotional), and neutral (not sales language). Avoid language that creates legal commitments: do not use "Counterparty warrants", "[Company] undertakes", "the Parties agree" in Recitals; these belong in operative clauses. If Recitals describe important factual assumptions (e.g., "Counterparty represents it holds all necessary regulatory licenses to perform the Services"), convert these into operative representations in Clause 33 or 34; do not rely on Recital statements alone. If Recitals describe [Company]'s capabilities, products or services, ensure language is factual and does not overstate or guarantee performance; prefer "[Company] provides a platform that enables..." over "[Company]'s platform guarantees..." If Recitals reference prior dealings, term sheets or LOIs, include "Entire Agreement" clause (Clause [X]) confirming this Agreement supersedes all prior understandings. Standard transitional language ("NOW, THEREFORE, the Parties agree...") bridges Recitals to operative clauses and signals that binding obligations begin in the operative sections. Business must finalize Recitals before execution and confirm they accurately and completely describe the transaction background; Legal must confirm Recitals are consistent with operative clauses and do not create collateral obligations.
counselNotes: Recitals are drafted jointly with Business, which provides the factual background and commercial rationale. Recitals must not contain operative obligations, service commitments, performance standards, guaranteed volumes or regulatory-status representations — those belong in the operative clauses. Keep recitals factual and non-binding.

title: Definitions and Interpretation
purpose: Precise definitions prevent costly post-signature disputes over contract scope and Party obligations. Undefined or poorly defined terms allow counterparties to expand obligations through interpretation, claim services or deliverables not intended, or deny obligations they originally accepted. In fintech and regulated services, ambiguous definitions create regulatory risk: if "Services", "Personal Data", "Customer Assets" or "Regulatory Requirements" are undefined or circular, [Company] cannot demon
fallback: Definitions in a Schedule. Defined terms may be set out in a Schedule rather than in a consolidated Definitions clause, provided that: (a) Clause [●] (Order of Precedence) states that Schedules form part of this Agreement and prevail over the main body in the event of inconsistency; (b) the definitions Schedule is version-locked at execution (dated, initialled by both Parties and incorporated by reference); and (c) defined terms are capitalised consistently throughout, and the Schedule is the sole source of those definitions.
redflags: Key operational or liability terms are undefined or defined so broadly as to be meaningless, including: [Services], [Losses], [Applicable Laws], [Personal Data], [Security Incident], [Customer Assets], [Change of Control]. Undefined terms allow counterparty to expand obligations by interpretation post-signature. Definitions contain operative obligations embedded within them (e.g., definition of "[Services]" includes "Counterparty shall perform all Services in accordance with Applicable Laws"). Operative obligations belong in operative clauses, not definitions. Embedding obligations in definitions makes them easy to overlook and difficult to enforce. Circular definitions (e.g., "[Services]" defined as "the services described in Schedule A", but Schedule A refers back to "[Services]" without further specification). Circular definitions create ambiguity and are unenforceable. Conflicting definitions across main body, Schedules, Statements of Work, Purchase Orders or other documents incorporated by reference, with no clear order of precedence. Conflicting definitions create interpretative disputes and allow counterparty to select whichever definition favours their position. Definitions
usageNotes: Before signature, Legal must check: (i) identify every capitalised term in the Agreement (main body, Schedules, Statements of Work, Purchase Orders, all incorporated documents); (ii) verify each capitalised term is defined exactly once with no conflicting definitions; (iii) check each definition for circularity (definition refers back to itself or another undefined term without adding substantive meaning); (iv) check each definition for embedded operative obligations (obligations belong in operative clauses, not definitions); (v) check each definition for scope expansion risk (terms defined so broadly that counterparty can claim obligations [Company] never intended); (vi) check each definition for unilateral update rights (external documents incorporated by reference that counterparty can change without [Company] consent). Do not permit liability-limiting terms (Force Majeure, Excluded Losses, Service Credits) or obligation-expanding terms (Services, Deliverables, Applicable Laws) to be buried in definitions with ambiguous or circular language; these must be clear, precise and enforceable. If definitions are placed in Schedules, verify order of precedence clause gives Schedules binding effect and Schedules are version-locked at signature. Run final audit immediately before execution to catch any late additions or amendments to definitions. Common errors to flag: "Services" defined by reference to undefined "Scope of Work"; "Losses" defined circularly as "all losses arising under this Agreement"; "Applicable Laws" defined as "all laws applicable to the Services" (too broad); "Security Standards" defined by reference to counterparty's unilaterally updatable policy document (unilateral expansion risk). Default rule: if any definition is ambiguous, circular, conflicting or contains embedded obligations, it must be redrafted and agreed before signature.

title: Contract Structure and Order of Precedence
purpose: Order of precedence clauses prevent post-signature disputes over which document controls when the Agreement comprises multiple documents (main body, schedules, statements of work, order forms, data processing addenda, incorporated policies). Without clear hierarchy, counterparties exploit ambiguity by claiming that their standard terms in a schedule, purchase order or click-through policy override negotiated protections in the main body, particularly liability caps, data security obligations, au
baseline:
Contract Structure and Order of Precedence.
(a) This Agreement comprises: (i) the main body (including the Recitals and all operative clauses); (ii) all Schedules, Annexes and Exhibits expressly forming part of this Agreement; (iii) any Data Processing Addendum or Information Security Schedule; (iv) any Statement of Work, Order Form or Purchase Order executed under this Agreement; and (v) any documents expressly incorporated by reference and version-locked at the Effective Date.
(b) If there is any conflict or inconsistency, the following order of precedence applies (highest first): (i) any written amendment executed by both Parties under Clause [●] (Amendment); (ii) the main body of this Agreement; (iii) the Data Processing Addendum or Information Security Schedule (for data-protection, security or privacy matters); (iv) any Statement of Work or Order Form (for the specific services, deliverables, timelines or fees in that document); (v) all other Schedules, Annexes and Exhibits; and (vi) any other documents incorporated by reference.
(c) No terms in any online terms of service, general terms of business or pre-printed terms of the Counterparty form part of, or vary, this Agreement unless expressly incorporated in writing by an authorised representative of the Company under Clause [●] (Amendment).
buyside:
Enhanced Precedence Protections. In addition to the Baseline order of precedence:
(a) the Company's policies and standards expressly incorporated by reference (including its Information Security Policy and Data Protection Policy) rank equally with the Data Processing Addendum for matters within their scope;
(b) the Counterparty's standard or pre-printed terms have no effect unless attached as a Schedule, expressly identified as incorporated, approved in writing by the Company, and version-locked at the Effective Date; and
(c) any document incorporated by reference is effective only as at the version in force on the Effective Date, and the Counterparty may not unilaterally update it in any way that expands the Company's obligations or reduces its rights or protections.
sellside: Supplier-Side Precedence. Where the Company is the supplier, this Agreement prevails over the Counterparty's order forms for all matters other than the pricing, volume and service parameters expressly stated in the order form, and the Company's product terms and acceptable-use and security policies prevail for use of the Platform.
fallback: Incorporation by Reference. A document may be incorporated by reference (by URL or citation) rather than attached, provided that: (a) it is available at a permanent, non-editable location stated in writing at execution; (b) it is version-locked by date, version number or checksum; (c) it has been approved by the Company before execution; (d) the Counterparty may not unilaterally update it without the Company's prior written consent; and (e) the Company retains a copy as at the Effective Date. Incorporation of a document "as updated from time to time", or by reference to its "current version", is not acceptable.
redflags: [Counterparty]'s terms or policies are incorporated by reference to a URL without version-lock or freeze date, granting [Counterparty] unilateral right to update or amend such terms post-signature, particularly where such incorporated terms address data protection, security obligations, liability limitations, audit rights, intellectual property ownership, termination rights or dispute resolution. No order of precedence clause, or precedence clause that is ambiguous, circular or internally inconsistent, leaving conflicts between main body and Schedules, or between Schedules, unresolved and subject to post-signature interpretation disputes. [Counterparty]'s online policies, terms of service, purchase order terms, invoice terms or standard forms are stated to prevail over the negotiated Agreement, or are incorporated without express [Company] Legal approval. Precedence clause states that "most recent" or "later in time" document prevails, creating risk that [Counterparty] can override negotiated protections by issuing subsequent purchase orders, order confirmations or policy updates with conflicting terms. Data Processing Addendum or Information Security Schedule is ranked below Statem
usageNotes: Demand an order of precedence clause in every contract structure comprising more than one document (main body plus schedules, order forms, statements of work, or incorporated policies). The standard hierarchy should be: signed amendments > main body > data/security addenda > order-specific documents > general schedules > incorporated policies, with protection that no subsequent purchase order, invoice term, click-through or online policy can override without express written approval. Version-lock all incorporated documents at signature by: (i) attaching them as Schedules; or (ii) referencing specific version number and date; or (iii) storing snapshot copy in contract file. Never accept incorporation by reference to "current version", "as updated", "from time to time" or URLs that [Counterparty] controls and can modify unilaterally; this allows [Counterparty] to expand [Company]'s obligations or reduce [Company]'s protections post-signature without renegotiation. Watch for vendor Master Service Agreements that state their standard terms prevail over separately negotiated statements of work or order forms; this structure allows vendor to preserve their template protections while diluting negotiated protections in transaction-specific documents. If [Counterparty] insists on referencing online policies or standards (e.g., ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS), version-lock the specific version of the standard (e.g., "ISO/IEC 27001:2022 as published October 2022") and state that updates to the standard do not automatically apply unless both Parties agree in writing. For Sell-Side transactions where [Company] is supplier, ensure Master Agreement prevails over customer purchase orders except for order-specific parameters (pricing, volume, timelines); this prevents customer from diluting [Company]'s liability protections through purchase order terms. Run precedence audit before signature: (i) list all documents forming the Agreement; (ii) identify all potential conflicts between documents; (iii) verify precedence clause clearly resolves each conflict; (iv) verify no unilateral update rights; (v) verify all incorporated documents are version-locked and approved. Common error: precedence clause omits Data Processing Addendum or states it ranks below Statements of Work, creating ambiguity when service levels conflict with data protection obligations (data protection should generally prevail). Default rule: if any document incorporated by reference is not version-locked or contains unilateral update rights, escalate to Head of Legal before signature.

title: SCOPE OF SERVICES, PRODUCTS AND DELIVERABLES
purpose: Precisely defined scope prevents post-signature disputes over what must be delivered, by when, to what standard, and what is excluded. Vague scope language ("all services necessary", "reasonable support", "as required") creates unlimited open-ended obligations that counterparties exploit to demand work, deliverables or support beyond what was intended or priced, generating cost overruns, resource conflicts and enforcement disputes. In regulated services, undefined scope creates regulatory risk:
redflags: Scope defined using unlimited or open-ended language such as "all services necessary", "such services as [Company] may reasonably require", "reasonable support", "industry-standard services" or "best efforts" without cap, exclusions, resource limitations, dependencies, assumptions or change control procedure. Such language creates unlimited obligation subject to [Company]'s unilateral interpretation and exposes [Counterparty] to scope expansion without additional compensation (or exposes [Company] to unlimited fees if [Company] is buyer). No acceptance criteria, acceptance procedure or acceptance timeline, or clause stating deliverables are "deemed accepted" upon delivery, passage of time or [Company]'s use, silence or failure to reject within unreasonably short period. This removes [Company]'s ability to reject non-conforming work and obligates [Company] to pay for defective deliverables. Scope expansion permitted by conduct, course of dealing, verbal instruction, email request or [Company] user action without formal change control procedure requiring written approval by authorized [Company] representative. This allows [Counterparty] to expand scope and claim additional fees based on infor
usageNotes: Every contract involving customer-facing services, regulated activities, personal data, customer assets, digital assets or production systems must have precisely defined scope with: (i) explicit inclusions (what must be delivered); (ii) explicit exclusions (what is not included); (iii) dependencies and assumptions (what [Company] or third parties must provide); (iv) acceptance criteria (objective tests for conformity); (v) delivery timelines with consequences for delay; and (vi) change control procedure (how scope can be varied). Use Statements of Work for complex, phased or multi-deliverable engagements; each Statement of Work should specify milestones, deliverables, acceptance criteria, delivery dates, fees and dependencies, and should cross-reference and incorporate the Master Agreement's liability protections, warranties, indemnities and termination rights. Include "time is of the essence" language for critical milestones where delay would cause material harm to [Company]'s business, regulatory compliance or customer commitments; this makes timely delivery a condition rather than merely an obligation, and failure to meet such milestone constitutes material breach justifying immediate termination. For Sell-Side transactions where [Company] is supplier, limit [Company]'s obligations to those expressly stated and exclude implied obligations, advisory duties, fiduciary duties and regulated functions not within [Company]'s license; this prevents [Counterparty] from claiming [Company] assumed obligations beyond what was negotiated or licensed. Watch for scope creep mechanisms: "reasonable support" (undefined), "industry-standard services" (subject to interpretation), "as reasonably required" (unlimited), "best efforts" (vague), "satisfactory to [Counterparty]" (subjective acceptance), "such other services as the Parties may agree" (informal expansion). All of these should be replaced with bounded, objective, measurable definitions or rejected. For services involving customer assets, personal data or production systems, verify scope explicitly states what [Counterparty] may and may not do: may process data for specified purposes only, may not use data for [Counterparty]'s own purposes, may not disclose to third parties, may not modify production systems without change approval, may not access customer assets except as expressly authorized. Run scope audit before signature: (i) list all obligations [Counterparty] assumes; (ii) verify each is express, bounded and achievable; (iii) verify exclusions cover activities [Counterparty] should not perform; (iv) verify acceptance criteria are objective and testable; (v) verify no unlimited or open-ended language; (vi) verify regulatory activities are confirmed as licensed. Default rule: if scope is ambiguous, unlimited or includes regulated activities not confirmed as licensed, escalate to Head of Legal + Head of Compliance before signature.
counselNotes: Use the high-level scope only for low-value, low-risk, non-critical engagements (for example, contract value below [USD 10,000], non-regulated, no customer data, no production systems, established vendor). Do not use it for regulated, customer-facing, data-processing, security-sensitive or production-critical services — use the Baseline or Buy-Side scope instead.

title: TERM, RENEWAL, EXTENSION AND EXPIRY
purpose: Term and renewal provisions control contract duration, lock-in periods and exit optionality. Automatic renewal clauses trap organizations in unfavorable arrangements by requiring affirmative action to exit rather than affirmative action to continue; missed notice deadlines trigger unintended multi-year extensions at counterparty-dictated pricing, often with retroactive price increases, minimum volume commitments or exclusivity obligations not present in the initial term. Automatic renewal introduces, imposes or reinstates minimum volume commitments, exclusivity obligations, non-compete restrictions, pricing increases or penalty clauses not present in Initial Term, locking [Company] into unfavorable commercial terms. Multi-year Initial Term (> 24 months) without: (i) termination for convenience right after [12] months; or (ii) pricing protection (fixed or CPI-capped); or (iii) performance conditions allowing termination for sustained non-performance. [Company] renewal option (Model 3) can be exercised only if Counterparty meets performance conditions, effectively giving Counterparty veto over [Company]'s renewal right. MODEL 3: DEFINED TERM WITH PLUANG RENEWAL OPTION
Strategic relationships where [Company] wishes to control whether to continue (e.g., key vendor relationships, technology partnerships, services where [Company] has negotiated favorable terms and wants unilateral right to extend). Gives [Company] continuation optionality without obligating [Company] to renew.
This [Agreement] shall commence on the [Effective Date] and shall continue in full force and effect for a period of [●] [months / years] (the "Initial Term"), unless terminated earlier in accordance with Clause [X] (Termination). Upon expiry of the Initial Term, this [Agreement] shall automatically terminate unless [Company] exercises its renewal option in accordance with Clause [x].
[Company] shall have the option to renew this [Agreement] for one or more additional renewal periods of [●] [months / years] (each, a "Renewal Term") by giving [Counterparty] written notice of renewal not less than [thirty (30)] days prior to the expiry of the then-current term. [Company]'s election to renew or not to renew shall be in [Company]'s sole discretion, and [Company] shall have no obligation to provide any reason or justification for its decision.
Unless [Company] and [Counterparty] agree otherwise in writing: (a) each Renewal Term shall be on the same terms and conditions as the Initial Term (or the immediately preceding Renewal Term, as applicable); (b) pricing for each Renewal Term shall not exceed pricing for the immediately preceding term unless [Company] expressly agrees to a pricing adjustment in writing; and (c) [Counterparty] shall not impose, introduce or reinstate any minimum volume commitments, exclusivity obligations, non-compete restrictions or similar limitations not present in the Initial Term without [Company]'s express written consent.
[Counterparty] acknowledges and agrees that [Company]'s decision to renew or not to renew this [Agreement] is [Company]'s business decision, and [Counterparty] shall have no right to compel renewal, claim damages for non-renewal, or seek injunctive or other equitable relief to prevent expiry of this [Agreement]. [Counterparty] shall plan its business operations and resource allocation on the assumption that [Company] may elect not to renew.
MODEL 4: DEFINED TERM WITH MUTUAL AGREEMENT FOR EXTENSION
Project-based arrangements, pilots, proof of concepts, high-risk or novel arrangements, regulated services requiring affirmative compliance sign-off, or arrangements where both Parties need to reassess and recommit at end of term (e.g., custody arrangements, joint ventures, strategic partnerships requiring Board approval).
This [Agreement] shall commence on the [Effective Date] and shall continue in full force and effect for a period of [●] [months / years] (the "Term"), unless terminated earlier in accordance with Clause [X] (Termination). Upon expiry of the Term, this [Agreement] shall automatically terminate and cease to have any further force or effect.
The Parties expressly agree that: (a) this [Agreement] shall not automatically renew, extend or continue beyond the Term under any circumstances; (b) any extension or renewal of this [Agreement] beyond the Term shall require a new written agreement executed by duly authorized representatives of both Parties; (c) continued performance, provision of [Services] or use of [Platform] after expiry of the Term shall not constitute renewal, extension or waiver of this Clause [x] but shall be governed by such interim arrangements as the Parties may expressly agree in writing; and (d) either Party may refuse to enter into a renewal or extension without cause, liability or penalty.
If either Party wishes to explore renewal or extension beyond the Term, such Party shall notify the other Party in writing not less than [ninety (90)] days prior to expiry of the Term. The Parties shall thereafter negotiate in good faith to determine whether to renew or extend this [Agreement] and, if so, on what terms, conditions, scope, pricing and duration. No renewal or extension shall be binding on either Party unless and until the Parties execute a written renewal agreement.
Each Party acknowledges and agrees that: (a) neither Party has any obligation, commitment or undertaking to renew or extend this [Agreement] beyond the Term; (b) either Party may decline to renew or extend for any reason or no reason, in its sole discretion, without liability or penalty to the other Party; and (c) the other Party shall have no right to claim damages, loss of profits, reliance damages, expectation damages or any other compensation or relief arising from or relating to non-renewal or non-extension.
Select term model based on: (i) service criticality (critical services should not use indefinite term or short-notice automatic renewal); (ii) strategic importance (strategic relationships where [Company] wants control use Model 3 - [Company] renewal option); (iii) vendor dependency risk (high dependency use Model 4 - mutual agreement, requiring affirmative recommitment); (iv) transition complexity (complex transitions require longer notice periods). For critical technology, regulated services, data processing, custody or infrastructure: avoid automatic renewal (Model 2) unless notice period is [ninety (90)] days minimum and termination for convenience right exists; prefer Model 3 ([Company] renewal option) or Model 4 (mutual agreement) requiring affirmative decision and adequate transition planning time. For routine services (SaaS, office supplies, non-production tools): Model 2 (controlled automatic renewal) with [thirty (30)] days notice is acceptable. For strategic partnerships or novel arrangements: use Model 4 (mutual agreement) requiring both Parties to recommit, preventing lock-in to arrangements that may not meet evolving business needs. Maintain renewal calendar for all contracts: diarize Initial Term expiry, notice deadline (if Model 2 or 3), and renewal review trigger date ([120] days before expiry for critical services, [60] days for routine services). For contracts with automatic renewal (Model 2), set calendar reminder [30] days before notice deadline; missed deadline locks [Company] into another term. For contracts with [Company] renewal option (Model 3), Businses initiates renewal discussion with Legal [90] days before expiry to confirm whether to exercise option; if exercising option, document decision and send renewal notice before deadline. For contracts requiring mutual agreement (Model 4), Business initiates renewal discussion [120] days before expiry to allow time for renegotiation if both Parties wish to continue. If counterparty proposes automatic renewal for critical services, negotiate for: (i) [ninety (90)] days notice period; (ii) termination for convenience right exercisable on [ninety (90)] days notice during any Renewal Term; (iii) pricing cap (CPI + [2-3]%) or requirement for [Company] written approval of increases. Run term audit before signature: (i) identify which model is used; (ii) confirm notice period adequate for service criticality; (iii) confirm pricing protection if automatic renewal or multi-year term; (iv) diarize expiry and notice deadline; (v) assign business owner for renewal decision.
Default rule: for regulated services, customer assets, personal data or critical infrastructure, reject automatic renewal (Model 2) unless [ninety (90)] days notice and termination for convenience right; prefer Model 3 or 4 requiring affirmative renewal decision by Business Approver and Head of Compliance sign-off.

variants.label: Model 1 — Indefinite Term
variants.text:
Model 1 — Indefinite Term.
This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues in full force and effect until terminated by either Party in accordance with Clause [●] (Termination). Either Party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by giving the other not less than [sixty (60)] days' prior written notice, without penalty or liability save for obligations accrued before the effective date of termination.

variants.label: Model 2 — Controlled Automatic Renewal
variants.text:
Model 2 — Controlled Automatic Renewal.
(a) This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for an initial period of [●] [months / years] (the Initial Term). On expiry of the Initial Term it renews automatically for successive periods of [●] [months / years] (each a Renewal Term) unless either Party gives written notice of non-renewal not less than [thirty (30)] days before the end of the then-current term.
(b) Unless the Parties agree otherwise in writing: (i) pricing for any Renewal Term is as stated in this Agreement or, failing that, the same as the preceding term; (ii) the Counterparty may propose a pricing adjustment for a Renewal Term on not less than [sixty (60)] days' written notice before it begins, which takes effect only with the Company's written acceptance; and (iii) all other terms continue unchanged.
(c) Where this Agreement governs critical services, regulated services, data processing, custody, payment processing or core infrastructure, the non-renewal notice period shall be not less than ninety (90) days.

variants.label: Model 3 — Defined Term with Company Renewal Option
variants.text:
Model 3 — Defined Term with Company Renewal Option.
(a) This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for [●] [months / years] (the Initial Term) unless terminated earlier under Clause [●] (Termination). On expiry it terminates automatically unless the Company exercises its renewal option.
(b) The Company may renew this Agreement for one or more further periods of [●] [months / years] (each a Renewal Term) by written notice not less than [thirty (30)] days before expiry of the then-current term. The decision to renew is in the Company's sole discretion, and the Company need give no reason.
(c) Unless the Parties agree otherwise in writing: (i) each Renewal Term is on the same terms as the preceding term; (ii) pricing shall not exceed that of the preceding term without the Company's written agreement; and (iii) the Counterparty shall not introduce or reinstate any minimum-volume, exclusivity or non-compete obligation not present in the Initial Term without the Company's written consent.
(d) The Counterparty has no right to compel renewal or to claim damages or equitable relief for non-renewal, and shall plan its operations on the basis that the Company may elect not to renew.

variants.label: Model 4 — Defined Term with Mutual Agreement to Extend
variants.text:
Model 4 — Defined Term with Mutual Agreement to Extend.
(a) This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for [●] [months / years] (the Term) unless terminated earlier under Clause [●] (Termination). On expiry it terminates automatically.
(b) The Parties agree that: (i) this Agreement does not automatically renew or extend; (ii) any extension or renewal requires a new written agreement executed by both Parties; (iii) continued performance after expiry does not constitute renewal or waiver and is governed only by interim arrangements the Parties expressly agree in writing; and (iv) either Party may decline to renew or extend without cause, liability or penalty.
(c) A Party wishing to explore renewal shall notify the other in writing not less than [ninety (90)] days before expiry, and the Parties shall then negotiate in good faith; no renewal binds either Party until a written renewal agreement is executed.
(d) Neither Party has any obligation to renew or extend, either Party may decline for any or no reason, and neither Party shall claim damages, loss of profits or other compensation arising from non-renewal.

counselNotes: Select the model by context: Model 1 (indefinite) for ongoing operational relationships needing exit flexibility; Model 2 (controlled automatic renewal) for routine, low/medium-criticality services where continuity is desired; Model 3 (Company renewal option) for strategic relationships where the Company controls continuation; Model 4 (mutual agreement) for projects, pilots, high-risk or regulated arrangements requiring affirmative recommitment. For regulated services, Customer Assets, Personal Data or critical infrastructure, reject automatic renewal unless the non-renewal notice period is at least ninety (90) days with a termination-for-convenience right; prefer Model 3 or 4 with Head of Compliance sign-off. Maintain a renewal calendar: diarise the Initial Term expiry and notice deadline; for Model 2, set a reminder [30] days before the deadline, as a missed deadline locks in another term.

title: CONDITIONS PRECEDENT
purpose: Conditions precedent prevent obligations from commencing before critical approvals, documentation, regulatory authorizations, security reviews or compliance controls are satisfied and verified. Starting performance before conditions precedent are met creates execution risk: if regulatory approvals are not obtained, vendor licenses expire, security assessments reveal material vulnerabilities, or AML/sanctions checks identify adverse findings, [Company] may be contractually obligated to perform or pa
baseline:
Conditions Precedent.
(a) Neither Party is required to commence performance unless and until all conditions precedent in Schedule [●] (Conditions Precedent) have been satisfied or expressly waived in writing by the Party entitled to their benefit. Each condition is for the benefit of the Party identified in Schedule [●], and only that Party may waive it.
(b) The Party responsible for a condition shall use commercially reasonable efforts to satisfy it by the date specified in Schedule [●] and shall provide the beneficiary with written evidence of satisfaction. No condition is satisfied by conduct, commencement of performance or passage of time; satisfaction must be confirmed in writing by the beneficiary.
(c) If any condition is not satisfied or waived by [●] (the Longstop Date), either Party may terminate this Agreement by written notice, whereupon: (i) neither Party has any further obligation to the other; (ii) any fees, deposits or advance payments are refunded in full within [thirty (30)] days; and (iii) neither Party is liable to the other for the termination, save for obligations accrued before termination.
fallback: Light-Touch Conditions (Low-Risk Engagements). For low-value, low-risk engagements with established counterparties, the conditions precedent may be limited to: (a) execution by both Parties of all contract documents; and (b) receipt by the supplier of any upfront payment or deposit.
redflags: Conditions precedent relating to regulatory compliance, security controls, data protection, AML/sanctions screening, customer asset protection or financial controls may be waived by conduct, deemed satisfied by passage of time, or waived without express approval from Compliance, Security, DPO or Finance teams (as applicable). Performance (particularly production deployment, data access, system integration or service activation) commences before mandatory regulatory approvals, data protection impact assessments, security reviews, AML/sanctions checks, compliance sign-offs or insurance verification are completed and documented, creating regulatory breach risk and operational exposure. Longstop Date is unreasonably short (< 60 days from signature) given the complexity and number of conditions precedent, preventing adequate time for regulatory approvals, security assessments or compliance procedures to be completed properly. No documentary evidence requirement for satisfaction of conditions precedent, allowing counterparty to claim satisfaction without objective verification. Business pressure to "go live quickly" results in waiver of security, compliance or regulatory conditions prece
usageNotes: Conditions precedent control go-live risk by ensuring all foundation requirements are satisfied before obligations commence; do not permit business pressure, commercial urgency or counterparty demands to override requirement for proper CP satisfaction, particularly for security, regulatory compliance, AML/sanctions or data protection conditions. Schedule [X] must list each condition precedent with: (i) objective satisfaction criteria; (ii) Party responsible for satisfying; (iii) beneficiary Party entitled to waive; (iv) deadline for satisfaction; (v) documentary evidence required. Before commencing any performance, Legal must verify in writing that all applicable conditions precedent have been satisfied and documentary evidence is on file; verbal confirmation or email assertions without supporting documentation are insufficient. For regulated services, customer assets, personal data or production systems, Compliance and Security teams must confirm satisfaction of regulatory and security conditions precedent before performance commences; Legal cannot waive these conditions without documented approval from relevant stakeholder. Longstop Date should be realistic given complexity of conditions: [60] days minimum for routine services; [90-120] days for regulated services requiring regulatory approvals or complex security assessments. If conditions precedent cannot be satisfied by Longstop Date, either Party may terminate without penalty; this protects both Parties from being locked into arrangements where foundation requirements prove impossible to fulfill. Watch for counterparty pressure to deem conditions satisfied or start performance "subject to" completion of conditions; this defeats purpose of conditions precedent and creates execution risk. Default rule: if any condition precedent relating to regulatory compliance, security, AML/sanctions, data protection or customer asset protection has not been satisfied with documented evidence, do not commence performance; escalate to Head of Legal + relevant stakeholder (Compliance, Security, DPO, Finance) for risk assessment and approval before proceeding.
counselNotes: Use light-touch conditions only for low-value, low-risk, routine engagements with no customer data, no production systems and no regulated activities. Where the arrangement involves production integrations, customer data, regulated activities, custody of Customer Assets or security-sensitive systems, retain and satisfy the full Buy-Side conditions precedent before performance commences.

title: ONBOARDING, IMPLEMENTATION, TRANSITION AND GO-LIVE
purpose: Implementation and go-live procedures control execution risk by ensuring services are properly deployed, tested and operationally ready before production activation. Premature go-live without completed acceptance testing, security validation, operational readiness confirmation and rollback planning creates service failure risk, security vulnerability exposure, customer impact and potential regulatory breach. Deemed acceptance upon delivery (or within unreasonably short testing periods) eliminate
baseline: ONBOARDING AND IMPLEMENTATION Each Party shall perform its implementation obligations strictly in accordance with the implementation plan, project plan or deployment schedule approved in writing by [Company] (the "Implementation Plan"). The Implementation Plan shall specify: (a) implementation milestones, deliverables and deadlines; (b) responsibilities of each Party; (c) dependencies and prerequisites; (d) acceptance criteria and testing procedures; (e) go-live criteria and approval process; and (f) rollback procedures. Neither Party shall deviate from the Implementation Plan without [Company]'s prior written approval. Go-live, production deployment, service activation or commencement of live operations shall not occur unless and until [Company] confirms in writing (by email from [Company]'s authorized representative) that each of the following conditions has been satisfied to [Company]'s reasonable satisfaction: all applicable conditions precedent set forth in Clause 6 (Conditions Precedent) have been satisfied and documented; acceptance testing has been completed in accordance with the acceptance criteria and testing procedures set forth in Schedule [X], and [Company] has provided written acceptance confirmation; all required approvals have been obtained from [Company]'s Compliance team (for regulated services), Security team (for production integrations or data access), Product team (for customer-facing features), Engineering team (for technical deployments) and such other internal stakeholders as [Company] may reasonably require; all defects identified during testing have been remediated to [Company]'s reasonable satisfaction, or [Company] has expressly agreed in writing to accept specific defects as known issues with documented workarounds; and rollback procedures, incident response procedures and support escalation procedures have been documented, tested and approved by [Company]'s technical and operations teams. For the avoidance of doubt, there shall be no deemed acceptance, implied acceptance or acceptance by conduct under any circumstances. Acceptance of any [Service], [Deliverable], milestone, implementation phase or component shall occur only upon [Company]'s e
buyside: Counterparty Implementation Obligations. [Counterparty] shall: deliver each implementation milestone, deliverable and phase by the date specified in the Implementation Plan, and immediately notify [Company] in writing of any actual or anticipated delay, together with proposed remediation measures; provide [Company] with all documentation, technical specifications, API documentation, integration guides, user manuals, training materials, test environments, sandbox access, test credentials and technical support reasonably required to enable [Company] to conduct thorough acceptance testing; remediate all defects, errors, bugs, security vulnerabilities, performance issues, data integrity issues and non-conformities identified by [Company] during acceptance testing, and re-submit for testing within [●] [business days] of receiving [Company]'s defect notice; provide a detailed rollback plan approved in writing by [Company]'s technical team prior to any production deployment, specifying: (i) rollback triggers and decision criteria; (ii) rollback procedures and timeline; (iii) data recovery procedures; (iv) business continuity measures; and (v) customer communication procedures (if applicable); not deploy, activate, release or promote to production any [Service], [Deliverable], system component, integration, API endpoint, database change or configuration change without [Company]'s express prior written go-live approval for each specific deployment; where implementation involves data migration, provide [Company] with: (i) data migration plan approved by [Company]; (ii) data mapping and transf
sellside: Counterparty Onboarding Obligations. [Counterparty] shall complete all customer onboarding requirements prior to [Company] activating [Services] or granting access to the [Platform], including: completion to [Company]'s reasonable satisfaction of all KYC/AML procedures, identity verification, beneficial ownership disclosure, source of funds verification and compliance documentation specified in [Company]'s onboarding procedures; completion of all technical integration requirements, API configuration, credential setup, webhook endpoints, callback URLs, IP whitelisting and other technical prerequisites specified in the [Documentation]; completion of user acceptance testing in [Company]'s sandbox or test environment and written confirmation from [Counterparty] that [Counterparty] has completed testing to [Counterparty]'s satisfaction; written acceptance by [Counterparty] of all applicable [Company] product terms, acceptable use policies, service level agreements and other standard terms governing use of the [Platform]; and payment of all required setup fees, onboarding fees or deposits. [Company] Right to Delay Activation. [Company] may in its sole discretion delay or withhold service activation, platform access or go-live pending: (i) [Counterparty]'s satisfaction of all onboarding requirements in Clause 7.7; (ii) completion of [Company]'s internal reviews, approvals and operational readiness procedures; or (iii) resolution of any security, compliance, operational or technical concerns identified by [Company]. [Company] shall have no liability to [Counterparty] for any delay in activatio
fallback: Where deemed acceptance is commercially unavoidable and [Company] determines that the risk is acceptable given the nature and criticality of the [Services], deemed acceptance may be acceptable only if all of the following conditions are satisfied: the acceptance testing period is not less than [ten (10)] [Business Days] following delivery of the relevant [Deliverable] or completion of the relevant milestone, and such period is extended by [five (5)] [Business Days] for each rejection and re-submission cycle; [Company] may reject any [Deliverable] or milestone by providing [Counterparty] with written notice specifying with reasonable particularity the defects, non-conformities or failures to meet acceptance criteria, and [Counterparty] shall remediate such defects and re-submit for testing; deemed acceptance applies only to minor, non-critical defects that do not materially affect core functionality, security controls, data integrity, regulatory compliance, customer experience or [Company]'s ability to use the [Deliverable] for its intended purpose; and deemed acceptance does not waive [Company]'s right to claim warranty breach, require remediation of latent defects discovered post-acceptance, or terminate for material breach if defects discovered post-acceptance constitute material non-conformity. This fallback is not acceptable for production integrations, security-sensitive syste
redflags:
Deemed acceptance upon delivery, or deemed acceptance within unreasonably short testing period (< [10] [Business Days]), eliminating [Company]'s ability to conduct thorough testing and reject non-conforming work.
No rollback plan, rollback procedures or contingency plan for production deployments, creating unrecoverable failure risk if deployment fails or introduces critical defects.
No objective acceptance criteria, allowing [Counterparty] to claim acceptance based on subjective standards ("to [Counterparty]'s satisfaction", "industry standard quality", "reasonable expectations").
Production integration, system deployment, data migration or customer-facing release proceeds without prior Security team review, penetration testing, security sign-off or Engineering team approval.
Acceptance criteria are stated in [Counterparty]'s sole discretion, subjective or based on [Counterparty]'s determination rather than objective, testable pass/fail criteria.
Implementation Plan permits [Counterparty] to unilaterally modify milestones, deadlines, scope or deliverables without [Company]'s written approval.
usageNotes: Acceptance criteria must be documented in Schedule [X] before signature and must be objective, testable, measurable pass/fail criteria (not subjective standards like "reasonable quality" or "industry standard"); criteria should be reviewed and approved by Legal, Engineering and Security teams before signing. For regulated product launches, customer-facing features, production integrations or data migrations, involve Compliance, Security, Product and Engineering in implementation planning and require written sign-off from each before go-live authorization. Implementation Plan should identify "critical milestones" where timely delivery is material condition (include "time is of the essence" language in Implementation Plan for such milestones); failure to meet critical milestone triggers material breach and termination right. Acceptance testing period must be adequate for thorough testing: minimum [10] [Business Days] for standard deliverables; [20-30] [Business Days] for complex integrations, security-sensitive systems or data migrations. Rejection notice must specify defects with reasonable particularity to enable remediation; vague rejection ("does not meet requirements") allows [Counterparty] to claim arbitrary rejection, so rejection notice should reference specific acceptance criteria that were not met. Rollback plan is mandatory for all production deployments and must be tested before go-live; plan should specify rollback triggers (what conditions require rollback), procedures (step-by-step rollback execution), timeline (how long rollback takes), data recovery (how to restore pre-deployment state) and customer communication (if customer-facing). For data migrations, require: pre-migration data quality assessment; data mapping and transformation rules; data validation and reconciliation procedures (comparing source vs destination record counts, checksums, key field integrity); post-migration validation report; and data rollback procedures (how to revert if migration fails). Never accept deemed acceptance for: production integrations, security-sensitive systems, regulated services, customer-facing features, or data migrations; these require express written acceptance following successful testing. If counterparty insists on deemed acceptance, negotiate for: (i) adequate testing period ([10-20] [Business Days]); (ii) right to reject with reasoned notice; (iii) limitation to non-critical defects only; (iv) preservation of warranty rights and latent defect remediation rights post-acceptance. Default rule: if implementation involves production systems, customer data, regulated services or customer-facing features, reject deemed acceptance and require express written acceptance after thorough testing; escalate to Head of Legal + Engineering + Security if business insists on accepting deemed acceptance for such implementations.

title: FEES, PAYMENT, INVOICING, TAXES AND SET-OFF
purpose: Payment provisions control cash flow, budget exposure and financial risk by establishing when payment is due, what must be delivered before payment, how payment can be disputed, and what rights exist to withhold or set off amounts. Unclear payment terms create budget overruns (automatic price increases without approval), premature payment obligation (payment before acceptance or delivery), uncontrollable liability (late payment penalties on disputed amounts), and inability to recover amounts owe
baseline: FEES AND PAYMENTS Fees and Charges. [Company] shall pay [Counterparty] the fees and charges set forth in Schedule [X] (Fees) (the "Fees"). Unless expressly stated otherwise in Schedule [X], the Fees: (a) are inclusive of all costs, expenses, charges, disbursements, overhead, administrative costs, materials, equipment, personnel, travel, accommodation and other costs incurred by [Counterparty] in performing its obligations under this [Agreement]; (b) are stated in [Currency] and shall be paid in [Currency]; (c) are exclusive of value-added tax, goods and services tax, sales tax, consumption tax or equivalent indirect taxes (collectively, "VAT"), which shall be payable by [Company] in addition to the Fees where applicable; and (d) shall not be increased, adjusted, escalated or varied without [Company]'s prior written approval. Payment Terms. [Company] shall pay undisputed Fees that are properly and correctly invoiced in accordance with this [Agreement] within [thirty (30)] days of [Company]'s receipt of a correct and compliant invoice. [Company] may withhold, deduct, set off or dispute any amount in good faith in accordance with Clauses 8.4 (Disputes) and 8.5 (Set-Off). Invoicing Requirements. [Counterparty] shall issue invoices in accordance with the invoicing requirements and procedures set forth in Schedule [X]. Each invoice shall: (a) be addressed to [Company Entity] at the address specified in Schedule [X]; (b) include [Counterparty]'s legal name, registered address, tax identification number and bank details; (c) reference this [Agreement] by agreement number, date and parties; (d) itemize all Fees, charges and expenses with sufficient detail to enable [Company] to verify the amounts charged; (e) reference the applicable Statement of Work, Order Form, Purchase Order or deliverable to which the invoice relates; (f) include VAT/GST breakdown and registration numbers where applicable; and (g) include all other information required by [Applicable Laws] for a valid tax invoice in the relevant jurisdiction. [Company] may reject and return for correction any invoice that does not comply with these requirements, and the payment period shall not commence until [Company] receiv
buyside: In addition to the Baseline payment provisions: Fee Increases Prohibited. [Counterparty] shall not increase, adjust, escalate or otherwise vary any Fee, rate, charge, expense reimbursement or other amount payable by [Company] under this [Agreement] without [Company]'s express prior written approval. Any purported fee increase without [Company]'s written approval shall be void and of no effect. Payment Conditional on Acceptance. [Company]'s obligation to pay any Fee relating to any [Deliverable], milestone, phase or other output shall be conditional upon: (a) [Counterparty]'s delivery of such [Deliverable] or completion of such milestone or phase; (b) [Company]'s acceptance of such [Deliverable], milestone or phase in accordance with the acceptance criteria set forth in Clause [X] (Acceptance); and (c) [Counterparty]'s compliance with all applicable requirements, specifications, service levels and standards set forth in this [Agreement]. [Company] shall have no obligation to pay for any [Deliverable], milestone or phase that [Company] has not accepted in writing. Audit Rights. [Company] shall have the right, upon reasonable prior written notice to [Counterparty], to audit, inspect and verify [Counterparty]'s billing records, time records, expense records, invoices and supporting documentation relating to any Fees charged under this [Agreement]. [Counterparty] shall maintain complete and accurate records for [●] years following the end of each calendar year and shall make such records available to [Company] and [Company]'s auditors during normal business hours. If any audit discloses t
sellside: Payment Due Date. [Counterparty] shall pay all Fees within [●] days of the invoice date (not the date of [Counterparty]'s receipt). Time is of the essence for payment obligations. [Company] may charge interest on overdue undisputed amounts at the rate of [●]% per annum (or the maximum rate permitted by [Applicable Laws], whichever is higher) from the due date until the date of actual payment, compounding monthly. No Set-Off or Withholding. [Counterparty] shall pay all amounts due under this [Agreement] in full without any set-off, deduction, withholding, counterclaim, defense or other reduction, except: (a) amounts expressly authorized by [Company] in writing; or (b) withholding tax required by [Applicable Laws], in which case [Counterparty] shall: (i) provide [Company] with not less than [thirty (30)] days' prior written notice; (ii) deduct only the minimum amount required by law; (iii) remit the withheld amount to the relevant tax authority within the time required by law; and (iv) promptly provide [Company] with an official withholding tax certificate or receipt issued by the relevant tax authority. Suspension for Non-Payment. If [Counterparty] fails to pay any undisputed amount by the due date, [Company] may (without limiting any other rights or remedies): (a) suspend provision of [Services], access to the [Platform] or delivery of any [Deliverables] upon [●] days' written notice to [Counterparty]; (b) charge [Counterparty] a late payment fee of [●] or [●]% of the overdue amount, whichever is greater; and (c) require [Counterparty] to pay future Fees in advance or provide a
redflags: Automatic price increases, escalation clauses or indexation formulas that allow [Counterparty] to unilaterally increase Fees without [Company]'s written approval, creating uncontrolled budget exposure and potentially exceeding approved procurement authority thresholds. No right to withhold, dispute, set off or deduct amounts, including for defective services, non-conforming deliverables, service level breaches, warranty breaches, indemnification claims or regulatory penalties arising from [Counterparty]'s breach. Payment required before acceptance, delivery or completion of [Services] or [Deliverables], obligating [Company] to pay for work not yet verified as conforming or complete. Late payment penalties, interest or fees that apply to: (i) disputed amounts pending good-faith dispute resolution; (ii) amounts withheld pending acceptance testing or delivery; or (iii) amounts set off against [Counterparty]'s debts or breach claims. No invoicing requirements or supporting documentation requirements, allowing [Counterparty] to invoice without itemization, time records, expense receipts or other verification enabling [Company] to validate charges. Prohibition on set-off or language requiri
usageNotes: Withholding tax treatment varies materially by jurisdiction: Indonesia (PPh Article 23 at 2% for most services, Article 26 at 20% for payments to non-residents), Singapore (15-17% withholding on payments to non-residents for services unless treaty relief), India (TDS at varying rates depending on service type and recipient residence), Philippines (various withholding rates depending on payee status and service type). Before signing cross-border payment arrangements, confirm with Tax team: (i) whether withholding tax applies; (ii) applicable rate; (iii) whether tax treaty relief available; (iv) documentation required (Certificate of Residence, Form 15G, W-8BEN-E); (v) remittance and filing deadlines; (vi) whether counterparty must gross-up or whether net payment acceptable. For Indonesia-governed contracts, confirm VAT treatment (11% standard rate) and e-Faktur electronic invoicing requirements; VAT typically added to Fees unless explicitly stated as VAT-inclusive. For Singapore-governed contracts, confirm GST treatment (currently 9%); GST applies if services performed in Singapore. For contracts >USD 100,000 annually, verify payment terms align with approved budget envelope and procurement authority thresholds before signing; automatic increases or uncapped liability may breach CFO-approved budget and require escalation. Payment conditional on acceptance is critical for deliverable-based contracts (software development, system integration, consulting projects); never agree to pay before acceptance unless advance payment is commercially necessary and amount is capped at reasonable percentage (typically ≤30%). Set-off rights are essential financial control mechanism allowing [Company] to recover service credits, breach damages, indemnification amounts, regulatory penalties and other [Counterparty] debts by deducting from amounts payable; never waive set-off rights without CFO approval. For contracts where [Counterparty] will invoice regularly (monthly services, usage-based pricing, expense reimbursements), specify detailed invoicing requirements: itemization by service/deliverable, time records (for hourly billing), expense receipts (for reimbursements), reference to applicable SOW/PO/budget code, and tax invoice requirements per local law. If [Counterparty] insists on late payment penalties, negotiate for: (i) reasonable rate (typically 1-2% per month or statutory rate, whichever is lower); (ii) exclusion of disputed amounts; (iii) exclusion of amounts withheld pending acceptance; (iv) no compounding; (v) cap on total interest/penalties. Before agreeing to advance payment (payment before delivery), assess counterparty creditworthiness and insolvency risk; if counterparty becomes insolvent before delivery, advance payment may not be recoverable. For sell-side contracts where [Company] is supplier, payment terms should favor [Company]: short payment period (15-30 days), interest on late payment, suspension rights for non-payment, prohibition on set-off (except statutory withholding tax), right to increase Fees on renewal. Default rule: if payment terms require [Company] to pay before acceptance, waive set-off rights, accept automatic increases, or accept uncapped late payment penalties, escalate to Head of Finance for approval; these create uncontrolled financial exposure requiring senior stakeholder sign-off.

title: SERVICE LEVELS, KPIS AND SERVICE CREDITS
purpose: Creates objective performance standards and remedies for operational failure.
baseline:
10.1  Service Levels. [Counterparty] shall meet the [Service Levels] set out in Schedule [SLA].
10.2  Service Credits. Where [Counterparty] fails to meet a [Service Level], [Counterparty] shall provide [Company] with the service credits calculated in accordance with Schedule [SLA].
10.3  Without Prejudice. Service credits are without prejudice to [Company]'s rights to damages, specific performance, termination and all other remedies available at law or under this [Agreement], unless this [Agreement] expressly states that service credits are the sole remedy for a specific, narrowly-defined service failure.
10.4  Reporting. [Counterparty] shall provide [Company] with monthly SLA performance reports and shall immediately notify [Company] of any material or imminent failure.
fallback:
Where counterparty insists on service credits as sole remedy, accept only if:
(a) the sole remedy applies only to specific, non-critical, narrowly-defined SLA metrics;
(b) data breach, security incidents, regulatory breaches, customer asset failures and wilful misconduct are explicitly carved out; and
(c) [Company] retains termination rights for chronic or critical failures.
redflags:
Service credits are the sole remedy for all service failures including data breach, security incidents, regulatory breach or customer asset loss.
No chronic failure termination right.
SLA exclusions (maintenance windows, third-party dependencies) are so broad they make the SLA meaningless.
No reporting obligation or root-cause requirement on breach.
usageNotes:
SLA metrics must be measurable, reportable and tied to remedies. Vague metrics are unenforceable.
For customer-facing and regulated services, SLA failures may trigger regulatory notification obligations. Ensure SLA breach is classified as a potential Security Incident or operational incident for notification purposes.
Diarise SLA performance reviews. Do not rely solely on vendor self-reporting.

title: PERFORMANCE STANDARDS
purpose: Sets general standard of care beyond specific SLAs.
baseline:
[Counterparty] shall perform its obligations under this [Agreement] with due skill, care and diligence, using appropriately qualified and experienced personnel, and in accordance with:
(a) good industry practice for services of the type provided;
(b) [Applicable Laws] and [Regulatory Requirements]; and
(c) the standards set out in this [Agreement] and any applicable Schedule.
buyside:
[Counterparty] shall perform all [Services] to the highest professional standards applicable to services of this type. For services involving regulated activities, data, security, customer assets, payment infrastructure or critical operations, the standard of care shall be that of a specialist provider in the relevant field operating in compliance with applicable financial services, data protection and cybersecurity requirements.
[Counterparty] shall replace any personnel whose performance does not meet the required standard promptly on [Company]'s request.
sellside: [Company]'s obligations are limited to reasonable skill and care applicable to [Company]'s role as [platform provider / data licensor / technology vendor] and are subject to the dependencies and assumptions set out in Schedule [X]. [Company] does not accept liability for outcomes dependent on [Counterparty]'s own systems, decisions or third-party services.
fallback:
For low-risk support or advisory services, the following is an acceptable fallback:
[Counterparty] shall perform the [Services] with reasonable skill and care and in accordance with [Applicable Laws].
redflags:
"Best efforts" by [Company] without control over outcome — do not accept without Documented Approval.
No personnel competency obligation for counterparty on critical or regulated services.
"As is" or "no warranty as to performance" for services involving customer data, assets or regulated functions.
usageNotes:
For technology, security, financial services or data processing vendors, require specific certifications (ISO 27001, SOC 2, etc.) and include them in Schedule.
Personnel replacement rights are critical for project-based engagements where named personnel are a material consideration.

title: COMPLIANCE WITH LAWS
purpose: Requires legal compliance without making [Company] responsible for counterparty compliance.
baseline: Each Party shall comply with all [Applicable Laws] that apply to it and its performance under this [Agreement]. [Counterparty] shall be solely responsible for compliance with all laws, regulations, orders and regulatory requirements applicable to its business, personnel, systems, services, licences and subcontractors, and shall not take any action that causes [Company] to breach applicable law.
sellside: [Company]'s compliance obligations under this [Agreement] are limited to those applicable to [Company] in its capacity as [platform provider / data licensor] under this [Agreement]. [Company] is not responsible for ensuring [Counterparty]'s compliance with laws applicable to [Counterparty]'s own business, operations or personnel.
fallback: Accept mutual compliance wording only if each party's obligations are separately stated and [Company]'s responsibility is limited to laws applicable to [Company] in its role under the Agreement.
redflags:
[Company] responsible for ensuring counterparty complies with all laws applicable to the transaction or counterparty services.
Broad "ensure compliance" obligations that extend beyond [Company] control.
Counterparty compliance obligations exclude financial crime, sanctions or data protection requirements.
usageNotes:
Cross-border contracts should specify which jurisdictions law applies to each party. Do not create a general obligation to comply with all laws in all jurisdictions.
Regulated and consumer-facing contracts require compliance review before signing.

title: REGULATORY COMPLIANCE AND COOPERATION
purpose: Preserves regulator-facing defensibility and cooperation rights.
baseline:
[Counterparty] shall:
(a) cooperate with [Company] and any [Regulator] in relation to any inquiry, audit, inspection, investigation, reporting obligation or request connected with this [Agreement], the [Services], [Personal Data], [Customer Assets] or [Regulatory Requirements];
(b) provide any information, documentation, records, access or assistance required by [Company] to comply with [Regulatory Requirements] within [5] business days of request (or such shorter period as required by law); and
(c) immediately notify [Company] if [Counterparty] receives any regulatory inquiry, investigation, audit request or enforcement action related to this [Agreement] or the [Services].
sellside: [Company]'s cooperation obligations with [Counterparty]'s regulators are limited to legally required assistance and shall not require [Company] to disclose information protected by legal privilege or confidential to [Company]'s customers. Requests for extraordinary regulatory assistance beyond routine cooperation shall be at [Counterparty]'s cost.
fallback: Accept cooperation obligations subject to confidentiality and legal privilege, provided that no restriction applies to cooperation with [Company]'s own regulators and the cooperation obligation cannot be used to block or delay regulator access.
redflags:
Counterparty may refuse or limit regulatory requests at its discretion.
Counterparty must consent to or approve any regulatory disclosure by [Company].
No obligation to notify [Company] of regulatory contact or investigation.
usageNotes:
Regulatory cooperation clauses are mandatory for regulated entities in Indonesia (OJK/BAPPEBTI), Singapore (MAS), Philippines (BSP/SEC) and India (RBI/SEBI).
MAS Notice PSN02, OJK and BAPPEBTI outsourcing guidelines require direct regulator access rights for critical functions.

title: LICENSING, PERMITS AND NO REGULATED ACTIVITY REPRESENTATION
purpose: Avoids unintended licensing exposure and clarifies regulated perimeter.
baseline:
Each Party shall obtain and maintain all licences, approvals, registrations, permits and authorisations required for its business and for its performance under this [Agreement]. [Counterparty] represents and warrants that it holds all licences required to provide the [Services] and shall promptly notify [Company] if any required licence is suspended, revoked, restricted, under investigation or not renewed.
Nothing in this [Agreement] authorises [Counterparty] to conduct regulated activity on behalf of [Company] or to hold [Company] out as the licensed party in respect of any activity carried out by [Counterparty].
buyside:
In addition to the baseline:
(a) [Counterparty] shall provide [Company] with copies of all required licences and authorisations before commencement of the [Services];
(b) [Counterparty] shall maintain the required licences in good standing throughout the [Term] and shall give [Company] at least [30] days' written notice of any renewal, variation, surrender or revocation; and
(c) if [Counterparty]'s licence is suspended, revoked or subject to enforcement action, [Company] may terminate immediately for regulatory reason under Clause [Termination for Regulatory Reason].
sellside: [Company] does not provide investment advice, legal advice, financial planning, tax advice, payment services, custody services, brokerage, dealing, or any other regulated service unless expressly stated and licensed by [Company] under this [Agreement]. [Counterparty] shall not represent [Company] as providing any regulated service that [Company] is not expressly licensed to provide.
fallback:
For low-risk non-regulated vendor relationships, accept:
[Counterparty] represents that it holds all licences required by law for its business and performance under this [Agreement].
redflags:
Counterparty assumes [Company] licence coverage extends to counterparty activities or shared services.
No warranty that counterparty holds required licences for regulated services, payments, digital assets, gold or custody.
No notice obligation for licence suspension, investigation or revocation.
usageNotes:
For digital asset, payment services, gold, custody, lending and financial services contracts, licence verification is mandatory before signing.
In Indonesia: BAPPEBTI (DFA traders), OJK (payment, investment management), Bank Indonesia (payment systems). In Singapore: MAS (capital markets, payment services, VASP). Philippines: BSP (EMI, payment systems), SEC (securities).

title: ANTI-BRIBERY, AML/CFT, SANCTIONS, FRAUD AND FINANCIAL CRIME
purpose: Controls financial crime exposure.
baseline:
Each Party shall comply with all applicable anti-bribery, anti-corruption, AML/CFT, counter-terrorism financing, sanctions, fraud prevention, market abuse and financial crime laws, including without limitation the UK Bribery Act 2010, the US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act 1977 and any applicable FATF standards.
[Counterparty] shall:
(a) not take any action that causes [Company] to breach such requirements;
(b) maintain adequate procedures and controls to prevent bribery, corruption, money laundering and sanctions violations in connection with this [Agreement]; and
(c) immediately notify [Company] of any actual or suspected financial crime, sanctions issue, AML/CFT concern or regulatory inquiry related to this [Agreement] or [Counterparty]'s business.
sellside: [Company]'s financial crime compliance obligations are limited to those applicable to [Company]'s own licensed business. [Company] may suspend or terminate this [Agreement] immediately if [Company] determines, in its reasonable judgment, that continuation creates financial crime, sanctions, AML/CFT or reputational risk.
fallback: Accept mutual compliance with immediate termination on breach, without requiring full audit rights for low-risk non-financial-services contracts.
redflags:
No sanctions warranty or AML/CFT obligation for counterparty in high-risk jurisdiction or conducting regulated financial services.
No beneficial ownership disclosure obligation.
No notification obligation for suspicious activity or regulatory inquiry.
Financial crime clause limited to "best efforts" rather than strict compliance.
usageNotes:
Financial crime provisions are non-negotiable. Do not accept carve-outs or limitations for regulated contracts.
AML/CFT controls are mandatory for all contracts involving payment services, digital assets, gold, custody, financial intermediaries and cross-border transactions.
UK Bribery Act applies to acts in connection with [Company] business regardless of jurisdiction. FCPA applies to US-connected transactions.

title: CONSUMER PROTECTION AND FAIR DEALING
purpose: Prevents misleading customer-facing terms and unfair practices.
baseline:
Where [Counterparty] communicates with, acts on behalf of, or affects [End Users] in connection with this [Agreement], [Counterparty] shall:
(a) ensure that all statements, materials, processes and conduct affecting [End Users] are accurate, clear, fair, not misleading and compliant with [Applicable Laws] and [Company]'s approved scripts or materials;
(b) not make any representation, commitment or product claim on behalf of [Company] that is not expressly authorised in writing by [Company]; and
(c) use only [Company]-approved materials for any customer-facing or marketing communications.
sellside:
[Counterparty] shall not:
(a) misrepresent [Company]'s products, fees, risks, licences, regulatory status or capabilities; or
(b) make representations about [Company]'s products to customers without using [Company]-approved materials.
[Counterparty] shall immediately take down or correct any inaccurate or unapproved materials upon [Company]'s request.
fallback:
For non-customer-facing, non-regulated vendor contracts, accept:
[Counterparty] shall not make any public statement or representation about [Company] or its products without [Company]'s prior written approval.
redflags:
Counterparty can make unapproved claims about products, returns, regulatory status, availability, customer protection or asset safety.
No approval process for customer communications using [Company] brand or products.
No complaint handling obligation or notification to [Company] of customer issues.
usageNotes:
Consumer protection laws vary across Indonesia (OJK consumer protection regulations), Singapore (Consumer Protection (Fair Trading) Act), Philippines (RA 7394) and India (Consumer Protection Act 2019). Specialist review required for consumer-facing contracts.
For regulated financial services, financial promotions and investment communications require specific approvals. Do not allow uncontrolled partner communications.

title: DATA PROTECTION AND PERSONAL DATA PROCESSING
purpose: Allocates data protection roles and compliance obligations.
baseline:
17.1  Role Allocation. Before processing any [Personal Data], the Parties shall document and agree the data protection role of each Party (controller, processor, data intermediary, personal information controller, personal information processor or equivalent under [Applicable Laws]).
17.2  Compliance. Each Party shall comply with all applicable data protection laws in relation to its processing of [Personal Data] under this [Agreement].
17.3  Data Processing Agreement. Where [Counterparty] processes [Personal Data] on behalf of [Company], the Parties shall enter into a Data Processing Agreement in the form set out in Schedule [DPA] before any [Personal Data] is transferred or processed.
sellside:
Where [Company] receives [Personal Data] from [Counterparty] or processes [Personal Data] as a [data intermediary / data processor], [Company] shall:
(a) process [Personal Data] only for the agreed purpose and on [Counterparty]'s instructions;
(b) implement security measures appropriate to the [Personal Data] processed; and
(c) subject to applicable law, assist [Counterparty] with data subject rights requests relating to [Personal Data] processed by [Company].
[Company]'s liability as processor is capped as set out in Clause [Limitation of Liability] except for obligations that cannot be limited by applicable data protection law.
fallback:
For low-risk non-personal-data contracts, accept:
Each Party shall comply with applicable data protection laws in relation to any [Personal Data] it processes in connection with this [Agreement].
However, any contract involving systematic processing, sensitive data, cross-border transfer or customer data must use the full DPA framework.
redflags:
No role allocation — data protection roles not documented before processing commences.
No DPA for processing relationships involving customer data, sensitive data or cross-border transfers.
Breach notification timeline longer than 48-72 hours for material personal data incidents.
Unrestricted subprocessing or cross-border transfers without [Company] approval.
No deletion/return obligation on termination.
usageNotes:
Indonesia: UU PDP No. 27/2022 — controller/processor concepts, consent, breach notification obligations and transfer restrictions. Verify implementation status.
Singapore: PDPA 2012 + PDPC Advisory Guidelines — data intermediary concept, 3 calendar days mandatory breach notification to PDPC.
Philippines: RA 10173 + NPC IRR — PIC/PIP roles, 72-hour breach notification to NPC.
India: DPDP Act 2023 — rules pending; verify implementation status immediately before use.

title: CROSS-BORDER DATA TRANSFER
purpose: Controls transfer of Personal Data across jurisdictions.
baseline:
No Party may transfer [Personal Data] outside the originating jurisdiction except:
(a) in accordance with [Applicable Laws] and this [Agreement];
