(b) using an approved transfer mechanism (adequacy decision, binding corporate rules, standard contractual clauses, or equivalent approved by the relevant data protection authority); and
(c) subject to prior written instructions or approval from [Company].
For the purposes of this Clause, "transfer" includes onward transfer by subprocessors and cloud service providers.
sellside:
Where [Company] transfers [Personal Data] in connection with providing the [Services], such transfers shall be:
(a) disclosed in [Company]'s privacy policy or the applicable customer-facing documentation;
(b) subject to safeguards required by [Applicable Laws]; and
(c) limited to countries and recipients necessary for the provision of the [Services].
fallback:
For cloud or SaaS services with standard global infrastructure, accept an approved subprocessor list with:
(a) advance notice of new subprocessors (at least [30] days);
(b) right to object within the notice period; and
(c) a termination right if the new subprocessor is not approved and no alternative is available.
redflags:
Unrestricted global transfer without disclosure or safeguards.
No onward transfer restrictions for subprocessors.
No data transfer impact assessment for high-risk or sensitive data.
Government access requests not notified to [Company].
usageNotes:
Indonesia: transfers from Indonesia require data subject consent or equivalent mechanism under UU PDP. Indonesian data localisation requirements for certain sectors.
Philippines: cross-border transfers require NPC registration or equivalent mechanism under RA 10173 for transfers to countries without adequate protection.
Singapore: transfers to countries without adequate protection require binding legal instruments under PDPA.

title: INFORMATION SECURITY AND CYBERSECURITY
purpose: Requires safeguards against unauthorised access, use, disclosure or compromise.
sellside: [Company]'s security obligations are limited to those relating to [Company]'s own systems and infrastructure as described in [Company]'s published security documentation. [Company] is not responsible for security failures caused by [Counterparty]'s own systems, integrations, credentials, personnel or third-party services.
fallback:
For low-risk non-data contracts, accept:
[Counterparty] shall implement industry-standard technical and organisational security measures appropriate to the [Services] and shall promptly notify [Company] of any [Security Incident].
redflags:
No security obligations for vendors with access to customer data, production systems, wallets, payment infrastructure or credentials.
No audit rights, penetration testing or vulnerability remediation requirements.
No breach notification obligation or timeline.
Access to production credentials, APIs or wallets without [Company] security approval.
usageNotes:
For critical infrastructure, payment systems, wallet providers and custodians, require specific certifications (ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, PCI DSS where applicable) and include as contract conditions.
Regulatory cybersecurity requirements apply to regulated financial services, payment systems and VASP operations in all [Company] jurisdictions.

title: SECURITY INCIDENT AND DATA BREACH NOTIFICATION
purpose: Ensures prompt notification and remediation of security events.
baseline:
[Counterparty] shall notify [Company] without undue delay and in any event within [24] hours after becoming aware of any actual or suspected [Security Incident] affecting [Company], [Personal Data], [Customer Assets], [Systems] or [Services].
The notification shall include:
(a) a description of the [Security Incident], the systems or data affected and the likely impact;
(b) the measures taken or proposed to address the [Security Incident]; and
(c) contact details of [Counterparty]'s designated incident response lead.
[Counterparty] shall provide updates at regular intervals and shall support [Company] in making any required regulatory, customer or third-party notifications.
sellside: [Company] shall notify [Counterparty] without undue delay of any [Security Incident] affecting [Counterparty]'s [Personal Data] processed by [Company], and shall cooperate in good faith with [Counterparty]'s investigation. [Company]'s notification obligations are subject to [Applicable Laws] and shall not require [Company] to disclose information that is legally privileged or would create security or enforcement risk.
fallback:
For low-risk contracts not involving Personal Data or Customer Assets, accept notification within [72] hours provided that:
(a) the 72-hour period aligns with applicable law; and
(b) [Company] retains the right to require immediate notification if the incident is material, customer-facing or likely to trigger a regulatory notification.
redflags:
Notification only after confirmation or legal determination — too late for regulatory compliance.
Notification timeline of more than 72 hours for incidents involving customer data, regulated operations or Customer Assets.
No cooperation with forensic investigation or regulatory notifications.
No cost-bearing obligation for counterparty-caused incidents.
usageNotes:
Singapore PDPA: mandatory data breach notification to PDPC within 3 calendar days where data breach is likely to cause significant harm or affect 500 or more individuals.
Indonesia UU PDP: breach notification obligations — verify specific timelines against current regulation.
Philippines NPC: 72-hour notification requirement to NPC under NPC Circular 16-03.
Internal escalation: Security Incidents must be reported immediately to Legal, Compliance and Security regardless of contractual notification timelines.

title: BUSINESS CONTINUITY, DISASTER RECOVERY AND OPERATIONAL RESILIENCE
purpose: Protects continuity of services and critical operations.
sellside: [Company]'s BCP and resilience obligations are limited to [Company]'s own controlled systems. [Company] is not responsible for [Counterparty]'s failure to implement adequate BCP or for failures caused by third-party infrastructure, cloud providers or force majeure events outside [Company]'s control.
fallback:
For non-critical, lower-risk vendors, accept a general obligation to:
Maintain and test business continuity procedures appropriate to the [Services] and provide evidence on request.
redflags:
No BCP/DR plan for critical, customer-facing or regulated services.
No RTO/RPO commitments for production systems.
No test evidence available or shared.
Step-in rights excluded for critical service failures.
usageNotes: MAS TRM Guidelines and OJK outsourcing regulations require BCP/DR obligations for critical outsourced functions. Include for all regulated and critical-dependency contracts.

title: OUTSOURCING, SUBCONTRACTING AND CRITICAL THIRD PARTIES
purpose: Controls delegation of obligations and third-party dependencies.
baseline: [Counterparty] shall not subcontract any material obligation under this [Agreement] without [Company]'s prior written consent. [Counterparty] remains fully responsible for the acts, omissions and defaults of its subcontractors as if they were [Counterparty]'s own. [Counterparty] shall flow down to each subcontractor all relevant obligations under this [Agreement] including data protection, security, confidentiality, compliance and regulatory cooperation obligations.
sellside:
[Company] may subcontract the performance of its obligations under this [Agreement] to [Company] Affiliates or qualified third-party providers, provided that:
(a) [Company] remains responsible for performance;
(b) subcontractors are bound by confidentiality and data protection obligations no less protective than this [Agreement]; and
(c) subcontracting does not alter the risk profile or regulatory status of the arrangement.
fallback:
Accept notification and objection rights (instead of prior consent) for non-critical subprocessors and subcontractors that:
(a) do not handle Personal Data, Customer Assets or production credentials; and
(b) are subject to [Counterparty]'s existing data protection and security obligations.
redflags:
Unrestricted subcontracting without [Company] knowledge or consent.
No flow-down of data protection, security, compliance or confidentiality obligations to subcontractors.
Counterparty not responsible for subcontractor acts, omissions or defaults.
Undisclosed offshore subprocessors handling Personal Data or Customer Assets.
usageNotes: Regulated outsourcing of critical functions requires MAS, OJK or applicable regulatory approval. Do not accept blanket subcontracting rights for regulated services without compliance review.

title: CLOUD, SAAS, API, PLATFORM AND TECHNOLOGY TERMS
purpose: Controls technology-specific access, dependency and operational risk.
baseline:
Access to any [Platform], API, software, application or cloud service provided under this [Agreement] is:
(a) limited to the [Permitted Purpose], [Permitted Users] and usage limits set out in this [Agreement];
(b) subject to [Company]'s technical documentation, security requirements and acceptable use policy; and
(c) revocable immediately by [Company] for breach of this [Agreement] or security risk.
[Company] retains all rights in its [Platform], APIs, data and documentation.
fallback:
For standard SaaS contracts after Legal/Security review, accept vendor standard terms where:
(a) data processing terms are aligned with [Company]'s DPA framework;
(b) termination and data export rights are expressly preserved; and
(c) liability and indemnity provisions meet the minimum thresholds approved by Legal.
redflags:
Unilateral changes to critical functionality or APIs without notice or opt-out.
No data export or migration rights — proprietary lock-in.
No security obligations or audit rights for technology services processing customer data or credentials.
Vendor may change, degrade or discontinue service on short notice.
usageNotes: For mission-critical SaaS and platform dependencies, evaluate vendor lock-in risk and ensure exit plan is documented before signing. Technical owner must confirm integration impact before Legal signs off.

title: DIGITAL ASSETS, GOLD, CUSTODY, WALLET, LIQUIDITY AND SETTLEMENT
purpose: Protects customer assets and regulated product perimeter.
baseline: Where the [Services] involve [Customer Assets], [Digital Assets], gold, custody, wallets, liquidity provision, exchange, payment, transfer, reconciliation or settlement infrastructure, [Counterparty] shall comply with all applicable regulatory, operational, segregation, safeguarding, reconciliation, recordkeeping and reporting requirements specified by [Company] and required by [Applicable Laws].
sellside:
Where [Company] provides non-custodial or informational [Services], [Company] expressly does not:
(a) hold, control, guarantee, underwrite, insure or safeguard [Customer Assets];
(b) provide investment, financial, trading, tax or custodial advice; or
(c) take responsibility for counterparty default, settlement failure, exchange outage or market conditions.
[Counterparty] acknowledges this disclaimer and shall not represent [Company] as a custodian, broker-dealer, settlement agent or guarantor.
fallback:
Narrower provisions may be accepted only where:
(a) no access to, control over, transfer of or settlement responsibility for Customer Assets exists;
(b) [Company]'s role is solely informational or technology-provisioning; and
(c) Legal and Compliance have confirmed no custody, settlement or regulated asset characterisation applies.
redflags:
Commingling of Customer Assets with counterparty proprietary funds.
Counterparty may impose liens, rehypothecate or reuse Customer Assets without written approval.
Reconciliation delayed beyond 24 hours for material discrepancies.
No segregation, key management or wallet access controls.
Counterparty or platform represents [Company] as custodian, adviser or asset guarantor.
usageNotes:
Always escalate to Legal, Compliance and Finance for any arrangement involving Customer Assets, Digital Assets, gold, wallets, private keys or settlement infrastructure.
BAPPEBTI (Indonesia), MAS (Singapore) and equivalent regulators impose strict asset segregation and safeguarding requirements. External counsel review is mandatory for regulated custody arrangements.

title: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY OWNERSHIP
purpose: Allocates ownership of pre-existing IP and newly created work.
baseline: Each Party retains ownership of its pre-existing [Intellectual Property Rights]. Except as expressly stated in this [Agreement], no right, title, interest or licence in any [Intellectual Property Rights] of either Party is transferred or licensed by implication, estoppel, operation of law or otherwise.
buyside:
All [Deliverables] specifically created for [Company] under this [Agreement], including work product, reports, code, configurations, integrations, documentation, data models and analysis, shall be owned by [Company] upon creation as a work made for hire (to the fullest extent permitted by law) or, where this characterisation is not available, [Counterparty] hereby irrevocably assigns to [Company] all rights in such [Deliverables] including copyright, database rights, patent rights and any other intellectual property rights. [Counterparty] shall execute any documents required to perfect or record such assignment at [Company]'s request.
Where [Counterparty] incorporates its pre-existing [Intellectual Property Rights] into [Deliverables], [Counterparty] hereby grants [Company] a worldwide, perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, non-exclusive licence to use such background IP to the extent necessary to use, maintain and exploit the [Deliverables].
sellside: [Company] retains all rights in its [Platform], software, data, algorithms, models, documentation, feedback, roadmap, enhancements and derivative works. [Counterparty] receives only the limited licence expressly granted in Clause [Licence Rights] during the [Term]. Feedback or suggestions provided by [Counterparty] relating to [Company]'s [Platform] or [Services] shall be owned by [Company] without restriction.
fallback:
Where vendor ownership of bespoke deliverables is commercially unavoidable, accept:
[Counterparty] grants [Company] a worldwide, perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, fully paid-up, non-exclusive licence to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, create derivative works from and sub-licence the [Deliverables] for [Company]'s internal and commercial purposes.
redflags:
Vendor owns bespoke work paid for by [Company] without granting a perpetual, irrevocable licence.
Implied licence only — no express grant.
Vendor may reuse [Company]-confidential requirements, data, product design or custom features for competitors.
Feedback or improvement suggestions automatically become vendor IP.
usageNotes:
IP assignment formalities differ by jurisdiction. In Indonesia, copyright assignment requires written agreement. In India and Philippines, moral rights may apply to certain creative works. Confirm with local counsel.
For AI, machine learning or co-developed technology, document IP ownership separately at SOW level before commencement.

title: LICENCE RIGHTS
purpose: Defines permitted use of IP, platform and materials.
buyside: [Company] requires, and [Counterparty] hereby grants, a worldwide, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty-free licence to use [Deliverables] and [Counterparty]'s background [Intellectual Property Rights] as embedded in [Deliverables], to the extent necessary for [Company] to exploit, maintain, modify and sub-licence the [Deliverables] for business purposes.
sellside:
[Company] grants [Counterparty] a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, revocable licence to access and use [Company]'s [Platform] solely for the [Permitted Purpose] during the [Term], subject to:
(a) compliance with [Company]'s acceptable use policy and technical documentation;
(b) payment of all applicable [Fees]; and
(c) immediate revocation upon breach, termination or suspension.
[Counterparty] shall not sublicence, resell, transfer or grant access to [Company]'s [Platform] to any third party without express written approval.
fallback:
Accept a broader licence scope only if it is:
(a) commercially priced and the risk is specifically assessed;
(b) limited to [Company]'s internal business purposes; and
(c) not broader than necessary for the specific use case documented in the SOW.
redflags:
Perpetual, unrestricted, transferable or sublicensable licence to [Company] brand, data, platform, algorithms, models or documentation.
Licence that survives termination for conduct not expressly agreed.
Counterparty may sublicence [Company] materials to third parties without consent.
usageNotes: Licence scope must match the actual integration and use case. Do not accept broad licences in template agreements without verifying that the scope matches reality.

title: WORK PRODUCT, DEVELOPMENTS, CUSTOMISATIONS AND FEEDBACK
purpose: Controls rights in project outputs and improvements.
baseline: All [Deliverables] specifically created for [Company] under this [Agreement] shall be owned by [Company] upon creation or, where earlier, upon full payment of the relevant [Fees], as specified in the applicable Statement of Work. [Counterparty] shall identify any background [Intellectual Property Rights] embedded in [Deliverables] in the applicable SOW.
buyside:
[Counterparty] shall:
(a) deliver all source code, assets, documentation and materials forming part of [Deliverables] to [Company] upon acceptance;
(b) obtain and waive (to the extent permitted by law) any moral rights in [Deliverables] on behalf of its personnel; and
(c) not use [Company]'s confidential requirements, designs, data models, specifications or product roadmap in deliverables for any other customer.
sellside: All feedback, suggestions, ideas and improvements provided by [Counterparty] relating to [Company]'s [Platform], services or products are assigned to [Company] without restriction. [Company] may improve, commercialise or modify its [Platform] based on [Counterparty]'s feedback without obligation or payment to [Counterparty].
fallback:
Accept vendor ownership of underlying tools or frameworks where:
(a) [Company] receives a broad, irrevocable licence for the specific use case;
(b) the tool or framework is identified as vendor IP in the SOW; and
(c) the tool is not specific to [Company] and is available to the vendor's other customers.
redflags:
Vendor owns bespoke, [Company]-specific deliverables paid for by [Company].
No source code delivery for custom-built integrations or platform-critical code.
Vendor may reuse [Company] confidential requirements, design concepts or product features for other customers.
usageNotes: Ensure each SOW clearly identifies: (a) what [Company] owns; (b) what vendor owns; and (c) the licence scope for each. Generic SOW language creates IP disputes post-delivery.

title: OPEN-SOURCE SOFTWARE
purpose: Prevents copyleft contamination and licence breach.
baseline:
[Counterparty] shall not include open-source software in any [Deliverable] in a manner that would require:
(a) the disclosure, licensing or transfer of [Company]'s proprietary source code, data or materials;
(b) restrictions on [Company]'s ability to charge for the [Deliverable] or its derivatives; or
(c) the application of any copyleft, share-alike or similar licence to [Company]'s proprietary materials.
sellside: Where [Company] provides software or platform access containing open-source components, [Counterparty] shall comply with all applicable open-source licence notices provided by [Company]. [Counterparty] shall not reverse engineer [Company]'s proprietary software or extract [Company]'s code from any delivered component.
fallback: Accept permissive open-source (MIT, Apache 2.0, BSD) if disclosed in the OSS inventory and confirmed not to contaminate [Company]'s proprietary code.
redflags:
Undisclosed copyleft (GPL, LGPL, AGPL) open-source embedded in Deliverables.
No open-source inventory or licence compliance warranty.
No security scanning or vulnerability remediation for open-source dependencies.
usageNotes: For software development, AI model training and platform integration contracts, open-source compliance is a mandatory diligence step. Engage Engineering for OSS scanning before acceptance.

title: AI TOOLS AND AUTOMATED PROCESSING
purpose: Controls use of AI tools with [Company] data, brand, IP and regulated content.
baseline: [Counterparty] shall not use, input, upload, expose or make available [Company]'s [Confidential Information], [Personal Data], [Customer Assets] data, [Intellectual Property Rights], content, materials or trade secrets to any artificial intelligence tool, large language model, generative AI system or machine learning algorithm without [Company]'s prior written approval in each case.
sellside:
Where [Company] provides AI-assisted or automated outputs as part of the [Services], [Company] disclaims liability for outcomes based on AI outputs that are:
(a) used for legal, investment, tax, regulated or medical decision-making without independent professional review; or
(b) inconsistent with [Counterparty]'s specific circumstances not disclosed to [Company].
[Counterparty] shall conduct independent verification of all AI-assisted outputs before reliance.
fallback:
Limited AI use may be accepted if:
(a) no [Personal Data] or [Confidential Information] is processed by the AI tool;
(b) all outputs are human-reviewed before use; and
(c) the AI tool is identified and approved by [Company] in writing.
redflags:
AI training on [Company] data, Personal Data, Confidential Information or IP without written approval.
Unreviewed AI outputs used for regulated decisions, customer communications, legal advice or investment recommendations.
No AI tools register or disclosure obligation.
usageNotes: AI regulation is evolving rapidly. This is a prudent internal control. Review AI clauses at each annual playbook update in light of applicable AI regulations in [Company] jurisdictions.

title: CONFIDENTIALITY
purpose: Protects non-public information and restricts unauthorised disclosure.
baseline:
Each Party shall:
(a) keep all [Confidential Information] received from the other Party strictly confidential;
(b) use [Confidential Information] only for the purposes of this [Agreement]; and
(c) disclose [Confidential Information] only to its officers, employees, directors, advisers and subcontractors with a need to know who are bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than this Clause.
Each Party shall notify the other immediately if it becomes aware of any breach of this Clause.
This Clause survives termination of this [Agreement] indefinitely for trade secrets and for [5] years for other [Confidential Information], unless the Parties agree otherwise.
sellside: [Company]'s confidentiality obligations are limited to information clearly marked as confidential or which a reasonable party would understand to be confidential given the context. [Company] may disclose [Confidential Information] to its Affiliates, advisers, regulators, legal counsel, auditors and service providers on a need-to-know basis without consent, subject to appropriate confidentiality obligations.
fallback: Accept a fixed duration of [3] years (not indefinitely) for ordinary business information. However, trade secrets, security information, customer data and personal data must remain protected indefinitely.
redflags:
Broad permission to use [Company] Confidential Information for benchmarking, competitive intelligence, AI training, marketing or product development.
No return or destruction obligation on termination.
No injunctive relief available for breach.
No survival clause — confidentiality expires on termination.
usageNotes:
For regulated entities, regulators may require disclosure of certain information. Ensure compelled disclosure carve-out includes advance notice to [Company] where law permits.
Confidentiality obligations in NDA should align with those in the main agreement. Check for conflicts.

title: PUBLICITY, ANNOUNCEMENTS, TRADEMARKS AND MARKETING REFERENCES
purpose: Controls public use of [Company] name and brand.
baseline: Neither Party may issue any press release, public announcement, marketing material, social media post, website content or investor communication that uses the other Party's name, logo, trademark, trade name, brand, products or relationship without prior written approval, except as required by law. Where disclosure is required by law, the disclosing Party shall give the other Party as much advance notice as reasonably practicable.
sellside: [Company] may identify [Counterparty] as a customer or partner in [Company]'s factual marketing materials where commercially appropriate, subject to compliance with the terms of this [Agreement]. [Counterparty] may not use [Company]'s brand or name in any context that could imply [Company]'s endorsement, warranty or regulatory status.
fallback:
Accept a limited announcement using approved text only, provided:
(a) the text is reviewed and approved by [Company] Legal and Comms before publication; and
(b) no regulatory status, endorsement or investment claim is made.
redflags:
Counterparty uses [Company] name, logo or brand in pitch decks, websites, investor materials, regulatory submissions or social media without prior written approval.
Counterparty implies [Company] endorsement, regulatory approval, exclusivity or investment backing.
usageNotes: Brand controls are critical for regulated financial services where counterparty communications may create regulatory risk or customer confusion. Always coordinate with Comms and Compliance before any public announcement.

title: NON-EXCLUSIVITY
purpose: Preserves [Company] strategic flexibility.
baseline: This [Agreement] is non-exclusive. Nothing in this [Agreement] restricts or limits [Company] from appointing, engaging, developing internally, acquiring or using any third party, alternative service provider, competing product, alternative solution or internal capability for the same or similar purpose, whether before, during or after the [Term].
buyside:
In addition to the baseline:
(a) [Company] retains the right to build, acquire or develop any competing or alternative capability without restriction;
(b) no minimum volume, minimum spend, preferred supplier status, most-favoured-customer right or referral obligation applies to [Company] unless expressly stated in Schedule [X]; and
(c) [Company]'s use or non-use of [Counterparty]'s [Services] shall not create any obligation or estoppel.
sellside: Nothing in this [Agreement] restricts [Company]'s right to offer the same or similar products, services or platform capabilities to any third party. [Company] may serve competitors of [Counterparty] and is not restricted in the development, marketing or provision of competing products.
fallback:
If counterparty insists on limited exclusivity, the following fallback is acceptable only with Head of Legal and business owner approval:
For a period of [X] months from the [Effective Date], [Company] will not engage [Category X] services from the named direct competitors listed in Schedule [X], provided that:
(a) the exclusivity is limited to [precisely defined scope];
(b) [Company] retains full termination-for-convenience rights; and
(c) the exclusivity expires automatically on [specific date or trigger].
redflags:
Broad exclusivity, de facto exclusivity through volume commitments or category restrictions.
Competitor restrictions that limit [Company] business or acquisition activities.
Minimum volumes or preferred status without approved business case and Documented Approval.
usageNotes: Exclusivity, MFN and minimum commitment arrangements are Escalation Required. Do not agree commercially without Head of Legal, Finance and Business owner sign-off.

title: EXCLUSIVITY, MFN, MINIMUM COMMITMENTS AND VOLUME COMMITMENTS
purpose: Controls strategic and financial lock-in.
baseline: No exclusivity, most-favoured-customer undertaking, minimum purchase, minimum volume, minimum revenue commitment, preferred supplier status, preferred pricing right, first refusal, right of first offer or similar restriction applies to [Company] unless expressly approved in writing by [Company] and stated in Schedule [X] (Commercial Terms).
sellside: [Counterparty] acknowledges that [Company] makes no commitment regarding volumes, referrals, allocations, or preferred status in connection with this [Agreement] unless expressly stated. Nothing shall create an obligation on [Company] to purchase minimum volumes or to meet any revenue target.
fallback:
If minimum commitment is unavoidable for pilot arrangements, accept:
[Company] commits to a minimum spend of [USD X] during the [pilot period of X months], subject to:
(a) [Counterparty] meeting all [Service Levels]; and
(b) [Company]'s right to terminate for convenience on [30] days' notice during the pilot period.
redflags:
Open-ended exclusivity without defined scope, term, KPIs or termination right.
MFN with audit rights over [Company] pricing across other customers.
Minimum spend commitment that continues beyond contract term or if Counterparty fails to perform.
Volume commitments without aligned performance conditions or exit rights.
usageNotes: Exclusivity, MFN and minimum commitments are always Escalation Required. Business teams must not agree these commercially without Head of Legal, Finance and business owner approval in advance.

title: NON-SOLICITATION, NON-CIRCUMVENTION AND RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS
purpose: Protects relationships while avoiding unenforceable overbreadth.
baseline: During the [Term] and for [12] months after termination or expiry, neither Party shall knowingly solicit for employment, hire or engage (whether as employee, contractor or consultant) any personnel of the other Party who was directly involved in performing this [Agreement], except through general public advertisements not specifically targeted at such personnel.
buyside:
For strategic partnerships involving significant investment, proprietary information sharing or customer introduction:
[Counterparty] shall not, during the [Term] and for [24] months thereafter, directly or indirectly approach, solicit or seek to divert from [Company] any customer, prospect, supplier or referral source identified to [Counterparty] specifically in connection with this [Agreement], without [Company]'s prior written consent.
sellside: [Company] shall be bound only by the mutual non-solicit in Clause [X]. [Company] does not accept any non-compete, non-circumvention, customer non-solicit or market restriction that would limit [Company]'s ability to conduct its ordinary business, serve existing or future customers, or make acquisitions.
fallback: Accept narrow employee non-solicit tied only to named or directly-involved personnel for a period not exceeding [12] months after termination.
redflags:
Broad non-compete that restricts [Company] from operating in any market, product category or geography.
Indefinite non-circumvention without defined scope or duration.
Non-solicit that restricts [Company] from engaging customers not introduced under this Agreement.
Penalties or liquidated damages for breach of non-compete that are disproportionate.
usageNotes:
Enforceability of non-compete and non-solicit obligations varies materially: Indonesia — generally unenforceable without consideration; Singapore — courts apply restraint of trade analysis; India — largely unenforceable post-employment under s.27 Indian Contract Act; Philippines — context-specific.
Always flag restrictive covenants to Head of Legal for review.

title: REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES - FUNDAMENTAL
purpose: Confirms the counterparty is a legally existing entity with authority to bind itself contractually. These representations address contract enforceability, not performance capability. If a counterparty cannot give these representations cleanly, the contract may be void or voidable regardless of commercial terms. Any qualification, hedge, or refusal to provide these representations is a material red flag requiring immediate disclosure of the underlying issue and escalation to Head of Legal. Legiti
redflags:
[Counterparty] qualifies or declines any representation without full written disclosure.
[Counterparty] proposes knowledge qualification for legal existence, authority or signatory authorization.
Board authorization stated as "pending" but execution proposed immediately.
Signatory identified only by given name, title or role, or authority shown as limited or conditional.
Disclosure of pending litigation, insolvency, regulatory investigation or enforcement affecting legal capacity.
Entity name, jurisdiction or status unverified against corporate registry.
Constitutional documents restrict or prohibit transaction type, value, term or jurisdiction.
usageNotes: This clause is mandatory for every contract regardless of value, term, transaction type, counterparty or commercial context without exception; even routine, low-value vendor contracts require Clause 35 representations in unqualified form. Before or at signature, request all three of the following: (i) certificate of incorporation or good standing from corporate registry; (ii) certified board resolution authorizing this Agreement and naming signatories by full legal name, or certified power of attorney, or other evidence acceptable to Legal; and (iii) constitutional documents (articles of association, bylaws or equivalent) showing no restriction on authority. Jurisdiction-specific requirements: Indonesia (certified notarized deed and NIB), Singapore (ACRA certificate plus certified board resolution), Philippines (SEC certificate plus certified board resolution), India (RoC certificate plus certified board resolution plus PAN). If counterparty cannot provide documentary evidence, do not sign; instead request written statement explaining which evidence cannot be provided, why (factual and legal reasons), underlying issue (litigation, board dispute, insolvency, regulatory prohibition), and proposed alternative evidence, then escalate immediately to Legal with counterparty's statement. If counterparty qualifies or hedges any representation, stop and do not proceed: unacceptable qualifications include "to our knowledge, we are duly incorporated" (legal existence is absolute fact, not knowledge-qualified), "board approval is pending" (cannot sign until finalized), "we believe the signatory has authority" (authority must be confirmed, not believed); borderline qualifications such as "entry does not violate law except as disclosed in Schedule X" require escalation to Legal (disclosure may be acceptable if immaterial or being remedied). Default rule: if uncertain, require all documentary evidence and escalate before proceeding.

title: BUSINESS AND COOPERATION REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
purpose: These representations address operational capability, regulatory compliance and performance quality. They allocate risk as between Parties for matters within [Counterparty]'s knowledge and control: regulatory status, compliance with law, quality and fitness of services, technical capability, conflicts and adverse proceedings. Unlike Clause 35 (invariably required unqualified), these may be negotiated according to transaction risk, leverage, value and criticality. Performance warranties for secur
buyside: In addition to the representations and warranties set out under Clause [35] above, the [Counterparty] hereby represents and warrants as follows: all systems, software, services and deliverables are free from: (i) material security vulnerabilities or defects; (ii) malware, viruses or malicious code; (iii) backdoors or unauthorized access mechanisms; and (iv) undisclosed data collection or monitoring mechanisms; it holds and maintains all regulatory licenses, permits and authorizations required to perform [Services], the services contemplated fall within scope of current licenses, it is in good standing with regulators, has received no notice of suspension or adverse action, and has not been subject to enforcement action within preceding twenty-four (24) months relating to [Services]; it is not subject to sanctions, is not owned or controlled by sanctioned persons, is not subject to AML/CFT investigation or financial crime enforcement, and has implemented adequate AML/CFT policies and controls; it shall process [Personal Data] in compliance with applicable data protection laws (PDPA, GDPR, CCPA, India DPDP Act, Indonesia PDP Law, Philippines DPA), has implemented adequate security measures (ISO 27001, SOC 2 or equivalent), shall process [Personal Data] solely as authorized and per [Company]'s instructions, shall assist with data subject requests, and shall notify [Company] within twenty-four (24) hours of any breach or incident; it maintains adequate insurance: (i) professional indemnity (minimum $[X]); (ii) cyber liability (minimum $[Y]); (iii) general liability (minimum $[Z])
fallback:
For low-value, low-risk contracts (value <[USD 50,000]; term <twelve (12) months; non-regulated; no customer data or digital assets):
[Counterparty] represents: (a) compliance with [Applicable Laws]; (b) [Services] conform and do not infringe; (c) personnel possess required qualifications. [Counterparty] shall provide evidence of authority and licenses upon request within ten (10) [Business Days].
Not acceptable for regulated services, digital assets, payment, customer-facing contracts, data processing or security-sensitive services.
redflags:
Disclaimer of performance or conformity warranties for regulated, data, security or customer-facing services.
No warranty re malware, backdoors or undisclosed data collection.
License marked "pending", "conditional" or "restricted" and [Services] may fall outside scope.
Represents licensing but refuses evidence or confirmation [Services] within scope.
Subject to sanctions or owned/controlled by sanctioned persons.
Regulatory enforcement or AML/CFT investigation within twenty-four (24) months undisclosed.
[Company] asked to warrant outcomes or matters dependent on third parties, market or customer behavior.
usageNotes: Select variant based on [Company]'s role: Buy-Side Variant for [Company] as buyer procuring critical services (system integration, data processing, cybersecurity, payment, custody), regulated counterparties, transfers of customer data or digital assets, or high-value transactions (>USD 100,000 or >24 months); Baseline Clause for [Company] as buyer procuring non-critical, low-risk services; Sell-Side Variant for [Company] as supplier (must confirm services within [Company]'s regulatory license per Compliance Handbook and include license suspension carve-out). Buy-Side warranties for security (malware-free), regulatory licensing, sanctions/AML, data protection and insurance are non-negotiable for critical services, regulated counterparties, data processing and security-sensitive systems; counterparty resistance to these warranties requires immediate escalation to Head of Legal plus relevant stakeholder (Compliance for licensing/sanctions, CISO for security, DPO for data protection, CFO for insurance). Acceptable Fallback only for contracts <USD 50,000, <12 months, non-regulated, no customer data, no security-sensitive systems, established vendors. If uncertain which variant or whether to accept counterparty qualification, default to Buy-Side Variant and escalate. After completion, verify consistency with Service Levels, Limitation of Liability, Indemnity, Data Processing, IP and Termination clauses.

title: DISCLAIMERS
purpose: Prevents unintended warranties and regulated advice.
baseline: Except as expressly stated in this [Agreement], no Party gives any warranty, representation or undertaking, whether express, implied, statutory or otherwise, to the maximum extent permitted by law, including any implied warranty of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose, accuracy, completeness, non-infringement, reliability, timeliness, security or uninterrupted availability.
buyside:
As [Company]'s buyer, resist any disclaimer that:
(a) contradicts an express warranty in this [Agreement];
(b) applies to regulated services, data, security, SLA, IP or indemnity obligations; or
(c) is broader than expressly necessary and operates as a blanket exclusion of all obligations.
fallback: Accept disclaimers only if express warranties and obligations are preserved and disclaimers do not negate the practical value of what was contracted.
redflags:
Disclaimer that nullifies all warranties including those expressly given.
Disclaimer used to exclude breach of data, security or regulatory obligations.
Consumer-facing or regulated disclaimers that violate applicable consumer protection or financial services laws.
usageNotes: Disclaimers are subject to mandatory law in all [Company] jurisdictions. Courts may not uphold disclaimers that are unfair, unreasonable or contrary to public policy, particularly for consumer contracts.

title: INDEMNITIES
purpose: Allocates third-party and specified losses to the party controlling the risk.
buyside:
In addition to the baseline, [Company] may:
(a) control the defence of any claim subject to the indemnity, using counsel of [Company]'s choice;
(b) require [Counterparty] to pay all reasonable legal costs (on a full indemnity basis) and investigation costs; and
(c) require [Counterparty] to indemnify [Company] for regulatory fines, penalties and sanctions to the extent permissible by applicable law and insurance.
sellside:
[Company]'s indemnity obligations shall be limited to:
(a) third-party claims arising from [Company]'s infringement of [Counterparty]'s [Intellectual Property Rights] by [Company]-provided materials;
(b) subject to the [Company] [Limitation of Liability] in Clause [X]; and
(c) excluding losses arising from [Counterparty]'s modifications of [Company]'s materials, combination with third-party software or use outside the [Permitted Purpose].
fallback:
Where counterparty resists a broad indemnity, accept an indemnity limited to third-party claims only, provided:
(a) [Company] retains direct loss recovery through breach of contract and termination rights; and
(b) the indemnity covers at minimum: IP infringement, data breach, security incident and financial crime breach.
redflags:
[Company] indemnifies counterparty for customer claims caused by counterparty conduct.
[Company] indemnifies counterparty for regulatory fines, penalties or enforcement costs arising from counterparty breach.
[Company] indemnifies counterparty for losses arising from counterparty negligence, fraud or wilful misconduct.
Indemnity is subject to a cap that applies to fraud, wilful misconduct or data breach.
usageNotes:
Full indemnity legal costs (solicitor-client basis) are recoverable in Singapore and certain other jurisdictions but not universally. Specify "full indemnity basis" in the clause where applicable.
Regulatory fines may not be insurable or indemnifiable in all jurisdictions. Verify with local counsel.

title: LIMITATION OF LIABILITY
purpose: Caps ordinary commercial liability while preserving critical carve-outs.
baseline:
Subject to Clause [Exclusions from Liability Cap], each Party's aggregate liability to the other Party under or in connection with this [Agreement] shall not exceed:
(a) the greater of [USD X] and the total [Fees] paid or payable by [Company] in the [12] months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim; or
(b) [in the case of a single incident] [USD Y],
whichever is higher.
buyside:
For critical services, data, security or regulated functions, the liability cap shall be:
(a) for general commercial claims: [12 months' fees or USD X, whichever is higher];
(b) for data breach, security incident or loss of [Customer Assets]: [USD Y] (super-cap); and
(c) uncapped for fraud, wilful misconduct, Clause [Exclusions from Liability Cap] matters and statutory obligations.
[Counterparty]'s liability cap shall not be set below [USD X] for any contract involving personal data, security, regulated functions or customer assets.
sellside: [Company]'s aggregate liability to [Counterparty] shall not exceed the greater of [USD X] and the [Fees] paid by [Counterparty] in the [6] months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim. Service credits are [Counterparty]'s sole financial remedy for SLA availability failures that do not constitute excluded liabilities.
fallback:
For lower-risk contracts where counterparty insists on a mutual cap below 12 months' fees, accept only if:
(a) the exclusion carve-outs (fraud, data breach, IP, regulatory breach) are preserved; and
(b) the cap is no lower than [USD X] for contracts involving data, security, regulated functions or customer-facing services.
redflags:
Cap applies to fraud, wilful misconduct, data breach, IP infringement, regulatory breach, payment obligations or Customer Asset misuse.
Cap set at a level that is manifestly insufficient to cover realistic loss scenarios for high-risk services.
Mutual cap that applies equally even though Counterparty controls the highest risk activities.
usageNotes:
Liability caps are subject to reasonableness and public policy analysis under applicable law. Caps may be unenforceable in consumer contracts (Indonesia, Philippines) and for certain statutory obligations.
UCTA 1977 (Singapore) applies a reasonableness test to liability exclusions in business-to-business contracts.

title: EXCLUSIONS FROM LIABILITY CAP
purpose: Preserves remedies for non-ordinary risk.
sellside: The carve-outs apply symmetrically. [Counterparty] may not cap its liability for customer misuse of the [Platform], breach of IP restrictions, breach of acceptable use or misuse of [Company]'s [Confidential Information].
fallback:
Where counterparty insists on capping some carve-out items, accept a super-cap (higher cap, not uncapped) for:
(a) data breach — if insurance coverage supports the super-cap amount; and
(b) confidentiality breach — if the super-cap reflects realistic loss scenarios.
Never accept a cap on fraud, wilful misconduct, Customer Asset loss or regulatory breach.
redflags:
No meaningful carve-outs — all claims subject to the general cap.
Fraud, wilful misconduct or Customer Asset loss subject to the general fee-based cap.
Carve-out for "gross negligence" removed by counterparty negotiation.
usageNotes: The list of carve-outs should be tailored to the specific risk profile of the contract. For digital asset, payment and custody contracts, Customer Asset loss and regulatory breach carve-outs are critical.

title: CONSEQUENTIAL AND INDIRECT LOSS
purpose: Controls remote and speculative damages.
fallback:
Accept mutual consequential loss exclusion where:
(a) direct losses are preserved for all key breach categories; and
(b) exclusions do not remove remedies for data breach, security incident, IP infringement or regulatory breach.
redflags:
Exclusion removes core remedies for breach of data, security, asset or regulatory obligations.
"Consequential" or "indirect" used to characterise losses that are actually direct and foreseeable (e.g. data remediation costs, regulatory fines).
Exclusion applies even to losses explicitly covered by a named indemnity.
usageNotes: Courts in Singapore and Indonesia have interpreted "indirect" and "consequential" loss differently. Define clearly which categories of loss are excluded rather than relying on labels.

title: INSURANCE
purpose: Provides financial backing for contractual risk.
sellside: [Company] makes no warranty that it maintains any specific level of insurance coverage. The existence of [Company]'s insurance does not expand [Company]'s liability under this [Agreement]. [Counterparty] is responsible for maintaining its own insurance coverage appropriate to its obligations.
fallback: For low-risk, lower-value contracts, accept minimum insurance at commercially reasonable levels without requiring [Company] as an additional insured, provided that cyber and professional indemnity coverage is maintained.
redflags:
No cyber or errors and omissions insurance for technology, data or security vendors.
Insurance stated as sole remedy or cap on contractual liability.
No notice of cancellation or change obligation.
Insurance coverage below realistic loss scenarios for the risk profile.
usageNotes: Insurance availability and requirements vary by jurisdiction. Indonesian vendors may not maintain international-standard cyber coverage. Consider compensating contractual protections where insurance is inadequate.

title: AUDIT, INSPECTION, RECORDS AND REGULATORY ACCESS
purpose: Ensures evidence, verification and regulator-facing access.
baseline:
[Counterparty] shall:
(a) keep complete, accurate and up-to-date records relating to its obligations under this [Agreement], including financial records, service records, data processing records, security logs, personnel records and compliance records;
(b) retain such records for at least [7] years after termination; and
(c) permit [Company], its authorised auditors and any [Regulator] to audit, inspect and verify compliance with this [Agreement] and [Applicable Laws] on [30] days' written notice (or immediately in the event of a [Security Incident], suspected breach or regulatory request).
sellside:
For [Company]'s sell-side, audit rights are limited to:
(a) verification of [Counterparty]'s compliance with usage restrictions, licence scope, data obligations and security requirements;
(b) annual frequency on [30] days' notice; and
(c) subject to confidentiality obligations for [Counterparty]'s other customers' data.
fallback:
For standard SaaS and low-risk contracts, accept:
(a) annual SOC 2 Type II or equivalent report in lieu of direct audit; and
(b) direct audit right triggered only by Security Incident, suspected breach or regulator request.
redflags:
No audit rights for critical, regulated or data-intensive services.
Regulator access blocked, delayed or subject to counterparty consent.
Audit limited to self-certification without third-party verification rights.
Records retention period too short for regulatory or litigation purposes.
usageNotes: MAS TRM Guidelines require direct regulator access for critical outsourced functions. OJK and BAPPEBTI have equivalent requirements. Do not accept contracts that limit or block direct regulator access.

title: REPORTING OBLIGATIONS
purpose: Requires operational, compliance and incident reporting.
sellside: Reporting by [Company] is limited to what is expressly agreed and included in the applicable [Service Level] or Schedule. No reporting obligation shall require [Company] to disclose information that is commercially sensitive, legally privileged or confidential to [Company]'s other customers.
fallback: Accept quarterly reporting for non-critical, lower-risk engagements. Mandatory minimum: incident reporting, material compliance breach reporting and material change notification.
redflags:
No reporting for SLA failures, incidents, asset reconciliation or regulated services.
Reporting obligations so vague or infrequent as to provide no meaningful oversight.
usageNotes: Reporting requirements should be operationally executable. Agree formats and frequencies with relevant internal teams before including in contract.

title: CHANGE CONTROL
purpose: Controls amendments to scope, costs, systems or obligations.
baseline:
No change to [Services], [Fees], [Service Levels], data flows, security architecture, subcontractors, regulatory responsibilities, integration design, operational dependencies or any material obligation is binding unless agreed in a written change order signed by authorised representatives of both Parties.
[Company] may reject any proposed change. [Counterparty] shall not implement any change that is not approved in writing.
sellside: [Company] may make non-material changes to the [Platform] (including updates, bug fixes and security patches) without [Counterparty]'s consent, provided such changes do not materially degrade the core functionality of the [Services]. [Company] shall give [Counterparty] [30] days' advance notice of material platform changes.
fallback:
Accept operational change notices (without formal change order) only for:
(a) administrative changes (contact details, notice addresses); and
(b) minor technical updates with no legal, commercial or security impact.
redflags:
Counterparty can change service scope, location, data processing, security controls or subcontractors unilaterally.
Email side deals or informal changes treated as binding amendments.
Counterparty can change pricing, SLAs or terms by posting updated online policies.
usageNotes: All change orders must go through Legal for review, regardless of how "minor" the business team characterises them. Changes to data flows, security architecture or regulatory scope require compliance sign-off.

title: SUSPENSION RIGHTS
purpose: Allows [Company] to stop activity where risk arises.
buyside: [Company] shall not be liable for any loss, cost, damage or claim arising from a good-faith suspension. The right to suspend is in addition to and does not limit any other right or remedy available to [Company].
fallback: Accept notice-and-cure before suspension only for non-critical, non-security, non-regulatory commercial breaches, with a cure period not exceeding [5] business days.
redflags:
No suspension right for security incidents, regulatory risk, sanctions or Customer Asset risk.
[Company] required to give advance notice before suspending for security incidents — creates dangerous delay.
Suspension limited to circumstances where [Company] can prove actual loss.
usageNotes: Suspension rights are a critical risk-management tool. Do not accept restrictions that prevent [Company] from acting immediately when security, regulatory or customer asset risk arises.

title: TERMINATION FOR CAUSE
purpose: Provides exit for breach and non-performance.
sellside:
[Company] may terminate this [Agreement] for cause on [30] days' written notice for:
(a) [Counterparty]'s persistent failure to pay undisputed amounts after demand;
(b) [Counterparty]'s breach of permitted use restrictions or IP restrictions; or
(c) any other material breach not remedied within the notice period.
fallback: Accept a cure period of [30] days for non-critical, remediable commercial breaches. The following must trigger immediate termination rights with no cure: fraud, sanctions, data breach, regulatory breach, insolvency, Customer Asset misuse and IP infringement.
redflags:
No immediate termination right for security incidents, data breach, regulatory breach, sanctions or Customer Asset misuse.
Cure period applies to fraud, wilful misconduct or irremediable breach.
Termination requires mutual consent or arbitration award before it is effective.
usageNotes: Termination rights must be operationally executable. Test the mechanism before signing: can Legal send the notice, is the correct entity identified, and what happens to Customer Assets and data on termination?

title: TERMINATION FOR CONVENIENCE
purpose: Provides strategic exit right.
baseline: [Company] may terminate this [Agreement] for convenience by giving [30/60/90] days' written notice to [Counterparty]. Upon termination for convenience, [Company]'s sole obligation is to pay undisputed [Fees] for [Services] properly performed up to the termination date. [Company] shall not be liable for any other loss, cost or damage arising from a termination for convenience.
buyside:
For buy-side contracts, insist on:
(a) a [30]-day convenience termination right for non-critical services;
(b) a [60]-day convenience termination right for critical or operationally complex services; and
(c) no early termination fees, break fees, minimum committed fees or wind-down costs, unless expressly agreed and approved by Finance.
sellside:
Where [Company] is the supplier:
(a) [Company] may terminate for convenience on [30] days' written notice;
(b) [Counterparty] may terminate for convenience on [90] days' written notice; and
(c) [Counterparty] shall pay all [Fees] committed and properly invoiced up to the end of the [Counterparty] notice period.
fallback:
Accept mutual convenience termination with [60] days' notice for non-critical contracts, provided:
(a) no early termination fee applies; and
(b) transition assistance rights are preserved for the notice period.
redflags:
No termination for convenience in long-term critical vendor contract without performance remedies.
Termination for convenience triggers large early termination fee, minimum committed fees or lock-in penalty.
Notice period for convenience termination exceeds [90] days without [Company] business justification.
usageNotes: Check exit rights before signing any multi-year contract. Termination for convenience is the primary protection against long-term vendor lock-in.

title: TERMINATION FOR REGULATORY REASON
purpose: Allows exit where continuation is unlawful or regulator-sensitive.
sellside:
Where [Company] is the supplier, [Company] may terminate or modify the [Services] immediately where:
(a) a change in law, regulatory guidance or [Company]'s licence conditions makes the [Services] impracticable or unlawful; or
(b) [Counterparty]'s use of the [Services] creates legal or regulatory risk for [Company].
fallback: Accept notice-and-consultation (rather than immediate termination) where the regulatory risk is not imminent and does not require emergency action.
redflags:
Counterparty consent required before [Company] can terminate for regulatory risk.
Regulatory termination triggers penalties, break fees or committed payment obligations.
No transition assistance following regulatory termination.
usageNotes: Regulatory termination rights must be preserved unconditionally for all regulated entity contracts. Regulators in Singapore, Indonesia and Philippines may impose fast-acting obligations that require immediate contract exit.

title: TERMINATION FOR SECURITY INCIDENT OR DATA BREACH
purpose: Provides exit for cyber and data risk.
baseline:
[Company] may terminate this [Agreement] immediately by written notice if:
(a) a [Security Incident] or breach of [Personal Data] materially affects [Company], its [End Users], [Personal Data], [Customer Assets], [Systems] or regulated operations; or
(b) [Counterparty] fails to notify [Company] in accordance with Clause [Security Incident Notification] or fails to remediate a [Security Incident] to [Company]'s reasonable satisfaction within [30] days.
[Counterparty] shall cooperate fully with forensic investigation and regulatory notification following termination.
buyside:
[Company] may additionally suspend access and initiate forensic investigation before deciding whether to terminate. [Counterparty] shall:
(a) not delete, alter or destroy any evidence relating to the [Security Incident] without [Company]'s written consent;
(b) cooperate with [Company]'s appointed forensic investigators; and
(c) bear all costs of investigation, notification and remediation attributable to [Counterparty]'s systems or conduct.
sellside: [Company] may terminate or suspend [Counterparty]'s access immediately if [Counterparty]'s systems, personnel or integrations create a security threat to [Company]'s [Platform] or [Customer Assets], including unauthorised access attempts, credential compromise or suspicious transaction patterns.
fallback: Accept a [30]-day cure period for minor security incidents that do not affect customer data, Customer Assets, regulated systems or require regulatory notification.
redflags:
No termination right until final legal determination of breach — delays response unacceptably.
Evidence destruction permitted before investigation is complete.
No forensic cooperation obligation post-termination.
usageNotes: Cyber incidents require fast action. Termination and suspension rights must be usable within hours, not days. Pre-agree escalation and response protocols with Security and Legal before contracts go live.

title: TERMINATION FOR INSOLVENCY, CHANGE OF CONTROL, SANCTIONS, ILLEGALITY OR REPUTATIONAL RISK
purpose: Protects against counterparty deterioration and adverse control changes.
sellside: [Company] may terminate for insolvency or sanctions designation of [Counterparty] without liability. [Counterparty] shall have no claim against [Company] for loss of anticipated profits, sunk costs or break fees following such termination.
fallback: Accept mutual insolvency termination rights. Resist broad subjective reputational risk termination against [Company] unless it is mutual, objective (by reference to specific triggers) and subject to a notice-and-cure period.
redflags:
No termination right on counterparty change of control — creates risk of contract with [Company] competitor or sanctioned entity.
Sanctions designation not an immediate termination event.
Counterparty acquired by competitor with no [Company] exit right.
usageNotes: Change of control provisions are critical for long-term or strategic contracts. Ensure change of control is defined broadly to include economic control, not just legal ownership changes.

title: CONSEQUENCES OF TERMINATION
purpose: Preserves accrued rights and manages post-termination obligations.
sellside:
Upon termination or expiry of [Counterparty]'s access rights, [Counterparty] shall:
(a) immediately cease all use of [Company]'s [Platform], APIs and [Confidential Information];
(b) delete all [Company] materials from [Counterparty]'s systems and provide written confirmation; and
(c) pay all outstanding undisputed [Fees].
fallback: Accept a [60]-day transition period for complex operational handover, provided services continue at current [Service Levels] during the transition.
redflags:
Termination releases counterparty from pre-termination breach obligations.
No data return or deletion obligation on termination.
Accrued indemnity, liability, audit or regulatory obligations extinguished on termination.
usageNotes: Termination mechanics must be operationally planned in advance for critical services. Include a termination checklist as a Schedule for complex arrangements.

title: EXIT ASSISTANCE, TRANSITION, MIGRATION AND DATA RETURN
purpose: Prevents lock-in and service disruption.
sellside: [Company] will provide [Counterparty] with standard data export functionality and migration support as part of the [Service] at the conclusion of the [Term], subject to applicable technical, security and legal limitations. Extended or bespoke migration support is available at [Company]'s published professional services rates.
fallback:
Accept paid exit assistance for ordinary services, provided:
(a) [Counterparty] cannot impose proprietary lock-in or block data access during transition; and
(b) rates for exit assistance are pre-agreed in the contract.
redflags:
No data export or migration capability — proprietary format lock-in.
Data deleted before migration is complete.
Exit assistance conditioned on payment of disputed amounts or waiver of claims.
Exit fees disproportionate or designed to deter exit.
usageNotes: Plan exit before signing. For SaaS and critical platform dependencies, validate export format, data completeness and migration feasibility with Engineering before contract execution.

title: FORCE MAJEURE
purpose: Allocates risk for events beyond reasonable control without excusing payment or preventable failures.
baseline:
No Party shall be liable for delay or failure to perform its obligations under this [Agreement] to the extent caused by a [Force Majeure Event] beyond its reasonable control, provided that:
(a) the affected Party gives written notice to the other Party promptly and no later than [5] business days after the [Force Majeure Event] arises, specifying the nature and expected duration;
(b) the affected Party takes all reasonable steps to mitigate the impact and resume performance as soon as practicable; and
(c) the affected Party continues to perform all obligations not affected by the [Force Majeure Event].
Force majeure shall not excuse:
(d) payment obligations accrued before the [Force Majeure Event];
(e) confidentiality, data protection, security, [Customer Asset] safeguarding or regulatory cooperation obligations; or
(f) obligations where the [Force Majeure Event] was foreseeable and preventable by the affected Party.
buyside:
For buy-side contracts involving critical services, add:
(a) [Counterparty]'s force majeure rights are limited where the event was caused or contributed to by [Counterparty]'s inadequate security controls, single points of failure or inadequate BCP;
(b) if a [Force Majeure Event] continues for more than [30] days, [Company] may terminate immediately without liability; and
(c) data, customer asset safeguarding and regulatory obligations continue regardless of force majeure.
sellside: [Company] is not responsible for force majeure events affecting third-party infrastructure, blockchain networks, exchange platforms, payment networks, settlement systems or cloud service providers. [Counterparty] accepts these risks where the [Services] depend on third-party infrastructure outside [Company]'s control.
fallback:
Accept mutual force majeure with:
(a) clear notice requirement (not less than [5] business days);
(b) mitigation obligation; and
(c) termination right if the event continues for more than [30/60] days.
redflags:
Force majeure excuses payment obligations, data breach liability, asset safeguarding obligations or regulatory cooperation.
Force majeure defined so broadly as to cover normal business risk, market downturns or supply chain issues.
No notice or mitigation obligation.
No termination right if event is prolonged.
usageNotes: Cyber incidents are generally not force majeure events where adequate security controls were not in place. Expressly exclude cyber incidents caused by counterparty negligence from force majeure.

title: MATERIAL ADVERSE CHANGE
purpose: Allows response to material deterioration in counterparty or transaction risk.
buyside: For long-term, critical or strategic contracts, include financial covenants requiring [Counterparty] to maintain minimum financial ratios or metrics and to notify [Company] immediately of any event that triggers or is likely to trigger an MAC.
sellside:
[Company] does not accept broad subjective MAC termination rights against [Company] by [Counterparty]. Any MAC termination right against [Company] must be:
(a) objective and limited to specific defined events; and
(b) subject to a [30]-day notice and cure period.
fallback: For shorter-term or lower-risk contracts, MAC provisions may be limited to insolvency, sanctions and regulatory licence loss.
redflags:
Broad subjective MAC right exercisable by counterparty against [Company] without objective conditions.
MAC defined so broadly as to cover ordinary market conditions, regulatory changes or strategic business decisions.
usageNotes: MAC provisions are most common in M&A transactions, financing arrangements and long-term strategic contracts. For ordinary vendor contracts, insolvency, sanctions and regulatory loss provisions are generally sufficient.

title: CHANGE IN LAW
purpose: Allocates cost and operational impact of legal and regulatory changes.
baseline:
If a change in [Applicable Laws] or [Regulatory Requirements] after the [Effective Date] materially affects a Party's ability to perform its obligations under this [Agreement], the Parties shall promptly discuss and agree necessary amendments.
[Company] may terminate this [Agreement] without liability, penalty or break fee where:
(a) continuation would be unlawful or contrary to [Regulatory Requirements] applicable to [Company];
(b) continuation would be commercially impracticable for [Company]; or
(c) the required amendments cannot be agreed within [60] days.
buyside: The cost of complying with changes in law applicable to [Counterparty]'s business, personnel, systems or services shall be borne by [Counterparty]. [Company] shall not bear compliance costs for obligations that apply to [Counterparty] as a matter of law.
sellside:
Where a change in law materially and demonstrably increases [Company]'s cost of providing the [Services], [Company] may:
(a) notify [Counterparty] of the impact and proposed fee adjustment; and
(b) if [Counterparty] does not agree to the adjustment within [30] days, terminate on [60] days' notice.
fallback: Accept equitable cost adjustment for changes in law that impose materially new and verifiable obligations on both Parties, where the scope and cost are agreed and documented.
redflags:
[Company] required to bear compliance costs for laws applicable to counterparty's own business.
Change in law termination requires counterparty consent or is not permitted.
usageNotes: Monitor legislative and regulatory pipelines in Indonesia, Singapore, Philippines and India for changes affecting [Company] group contracts. Flag relevant changes to Head of Legal.

title: ASSIGNMENT, NOVATION, TRANSFER AND CHANGE OF CONTROL
purpose: Controls transfer of rights and obligations.
baseline:
Neither Party may assign, novate, transfer, sub-licence or otherwise deal with its rights or obligations under this [Agreement] without the prior written consent of the other Party, except that [Company] may assign or transfer its rights and obligations to:
(a) a [Company] [Affiliate];
(b) a successor entity following a merger, reorganisation or transfer of all or substantially all of [Company]'s business to which this [Agreement] relates; or
(c) as required in connection with financing, securitisation or group restructuring.
Any purported assignment in breach of this Clause is void.
buyside:
In addition:
(a) [Counterparty] shall not assign or transfer to a [Company] competitor, a sanctioned entity, or an entity that creates legal, regulatory or reputational risk for [Company];
(b) a [Change of Control] of [Counterparty] shall be treated as an assignment requiring [Company]'s consent; and
(c) [Company] may withhold consent to any assignment where [Company] determines, in its reasonable judgment, that the proposed assignee does not meet [Company]'s due diligence, regulatory or security standards.
sellside: [Company] may assign or transfer its rights and obligations to any [Company] entity or any successor as part of a group reorganisation without consent. [Counterparty] shall not assign, transfer, novate or subcontract its obligations without [Company]'s prior written consent.
fallback: Accept assignment to existing [Company] affiliates or intra-group restructuring without consent. Accept counterparty assignment to a non-competitor that demonstrates equivalent capability and creditworthiness, subject to [Company]'s right to conduct due diligence.
redflags:
Counterparty may freely assign to a [Company] competitor, offshore entity, insolvent affiliate or unvetted subcontractor.
Restrictions on [Company] group assignment that prevent legitimate reorganisation or financing.
usageNotes: Assignment clauses are particularly important for data processing, regulated services and customer-facing arrangements where the identity of the counterparty is material.

title: RELATIONSHIP OF PARTIES; NO PARTNERSHIP, AGENCY OR FIDUCIARY DUTY
purpose: Prevents unintended authority or regulated characterisation.
baseline: The Parties are independent contractors. Nothing in this [Agreement] creates or is intended to create a partnership, joint venture, employment relationship, agency, trust, fiduciary relationship, association, or any authority for either Party to bind, represent or act on behalf of the other Party, unless expressly stated.
sellside: [Company] does not provide investment advice, financial planning, tax advice, custodial services, brokerage, dealing, trust services, fiduciary services or any other regulated or advisory service to [Counterparty] through this [Agreement] unless expressly and separately agreed and licensed.
fallback: For referral, marketing and introducer arrangements, add express limitations on [Counterparty]'s authority to make regulated statements, financial promotions or product claims on behalf of [Company].
redflags:
Counterparty may act as [Company] agent or bind [Company] without express written controls.
Agreement creates de facto fiduciary duty, trust or investment management relationship by conduct.
usageNotes: For regulated financial services, the relationship characterisation affects licensing and regulatory perimeter. Always involve Compliance and Legal before signing arrangements where Counterparty interacts with customers on [Company]'s behalf.

title: NOTICES
purpose: Ensures legally effective communications.
buyside:
All formal notices (including breach notices, termination notices, claims and regulatory notices) shall be copied to:
[Company] Legal: [legal@[company-domain] or as updated by [Company]]
[Counterparty]'s General Counsel or Legal Department: [address]
Notices sent to business contacts only (without Legal copy) shall not be effective for formal breach, termination or claim purposes.
sellside: [Company] may issue operational notices (including SLA reports, invoices, product updates and non-material communications) by email to [Counterparty]'s designated operational contact. Formal breach, termination, indemnity and regulatory notices require the formal notice procedure above.
fallback: Accept email notices for ordinary communications. Require copy to Legal for all notices of breach, termination, claim or regulatory matter.
redflags:
Notice only to business user without Legal copy for termination, breach or claim.
Notice sent to personal email, informal channel or outdated address.
Deemed notice rules that make notice effective before actual delivery (e.g. 3 days after posting to a disputed address).
usageNotes: Include Legal as a mandatory copy recipient for all formal notices in every contract. Ensure notice addresses are updated each time personnel changes.

title: ENTIRE AGREEMENT
purpose: Prevents reliance on prior statements outside the contract.
baseline:
This [Agreement] constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to its subject matter and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, proposals, negotiations, representations, warranties and communications, whether oral or written, relating to its subject matter.
Each Party acknowledges that it has not relied on any representation, warranty or statement not expressly set out in this [Agreement] in entering into it, except that this Clause does not limit or exclude liability for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation.
buyside: [Company] has not relied on any product claims, technology performance guarantees, regulatory assurances, feasibility statements, reference implementations or marketing materials provided by [Counterparty] that are not expressly included in this [Agreement]. Any such representations shall be documented in a Schedule or warranty in this [Agreement] before signing.
sellside: [Counterparty] has not relied on any representations by [Company] about anticipated usage volumes, revenue projections, customer acquisition, market performance or business outcomes that are not expressly stated in this [Agreement].
fallback:
Accept standard entire agreement clause if:
(a) fraud carve-out is preserved; and
(b) all agreed business terms are documented in the contract before signing.
redflags:
Counterparty relies on sales representations, pitch materials, demos or external statements not in the contract.
No fraud carve-out — entire agreement clause used to exclude liability for pre-contractual misrepresentation.
usageNotes: Before signing, ensure all agreed commercial terms (pricing, service scope, SLA, milestones, key personnel) are documented in the Agreement or a Schedule. Do not rely on email side arrangements.

title: AMENDMENTS AND VARIATIONS
purpose: Prevents informal or unauthorised contract changes.
baseline: No amendment, modification, variation, waiver or supplementation of this [Agreement] is valid or binding unless made in writing and signed by an authorised representative of each Party. No act, omission, conduct or course of dealing shall constitute an amendment or waiver unless documented in accordance with this Clause.
buyside:
Amendments affecting price, scope, [Service Levels], liability, data flows, security architecture, regulatory obligations, subcontracting or any other material term require:
(a) [Company] Legal review and sign-off; and
(b) signature by a signatory with authority under [Company]'s delegation of authority.
[Company] does not accept "click-to-accept" or "continuing to use the Service" as a mechanism for amending negotiated contractual terms.
sellside: [Company] may amend its acceptable use policy, security requirements and platform policies on [30] days' notice. Amendments to negotiated core terms (pricing, liability, IP, data, termination) require mutual written agreement.
fallback:
Accept change orders for operational scope if:
(a) signed by authorised representatives; and
(b) the change does not affect legal, regulatory, security, liability or pricing terms.
redflags:
Oral amendments, email side deals or platform policy updates binding as contract amendments.
Unilateral changes to core terms (pricing, liability, data processing, SLAs) allowed by contract.
Click-to-accept updates to platform terms overriding negotiated commercial agreement.
usageNotes: Review material change requests through the same process as the original contract. Business teams must not agree commercial amendments casually without Legal sign-off.

title: WAIVER
purpose: Prevents loss of rights through delay or partial enforcement.
baseline:
No failure or delay by either Party in exercising any right, power or remedy under this [Agreement] shall operate as a waiver of that right. No single or partial exercise of any right, power or remedy precludes any other or further exercise of that right or any other right. Any waiver of a breach does not waive any subsequent breach.
A waiver is effective only if made in writing and signed by an authorised representative of the waiving Party, and applies only to the specific circumstances and instance expressly stated.
buyside: Same as baseline. Preserve cumulative remedies and ensure waiver cannot be implied from course of dealing, forbearance, delay, payment acceptance or partial enforcement.
sellside: Same as baseline. [Company]'s acceptance of payment, continued provision of [Services] or forbearance from enforcement shall not constitute a waiver of any right.
fallback: Accept standard no-waiver clause as baseline.
redflags:
Broad waiver implied by conduct, course of dealing, delay or payment acceptance.
Waiver of one breach stated to operate as waiver of all future breaches.
usageNotes: No-waiver clauses protect [Company] from losing rights through operational necessity. Ensure they are included in every contract.

title: SEVERABILITY
purpose: Preserves remainder of contract if one provision is invalid.
baseline:
If any provision of this [Agreement] is found to be invalid, illegal or unenforceable by any court or tribunal of competent jurisdiction, that provision shall be:
(a) modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid, legal and enforceable; or
(b) deleted if modification is not possible,
and the remainder of this [Agreement] shall continue in full force and effect.
The Parties shall use reasonable efforts to agree a replacement provision that achieves, as closely as possible, the original commercial intent and effect of the deleted provision.
