buyside: Same as baseline. Include a "blue pencil" qualifier where available under applicable law to allow courts to modify rather than delete non-compliant provisions (particularly for restraint of trade and non-compete clauses).
sellside: Same as baseline.
fallback: Accept standard severability clause.
redflags:
Invalid provision voids the entire Agreement unless required by law.
No obligation to replace deleted provision — leaves gaps in key protections.
usageNotes: Severability is particularly important for non-compete, non-solicit and restrictive covenant provisions, which courts may blue-pencil or modify in some jurisdictions rather than striking entirely.

title: FURTHER ASSURANCE
purpose: Requires cooperation to implement the transaction.
baseline: Each Party shall promptly execute and deliver all documents and take all actions reasonably necessary or desirable to give full effect to this [Agreement] and the transactions contemplated by it.
buyside: For IP assignments, regulatory filings, data migrations, security transitions and asset transfers, include a specific further assurance obligation with a timeline for completion and a right for [Company] to execute documents on [Counterparty]'s behalf as attorney-in-fact if [Counterparty] fails to act within [10] business days of request.
sellside: [Company]'s further assurance obligations are limited to acts within [Company]'s reasonable control and shall not require [Company] to incur material costs, make regulatory filings on [Counterparty]'s behalf, or take actions inconsistent with [Company]'s regulatory or legal obligations.
fallback: Accept standard further assurance clause bounded by reasonable acts within the Party's control.
redflags:
Open-ended obligation to do anything requested without scope limitation or cost control.
Further assurance used to create new licences, filings or obligations not in the original Agreement.
usageNotes: Useful for IP assignment perfection, corporate filings and regulatory notifications. Keep bounded — should not be used to create obligations beyond what was agreed.

title: CUMULATIVE REMEDIES
purpose: Preserves all available remedies.
baseline: Rights and remedies under this [Agreement] are cumulative and are not exclusive of any other rights or remedies provided by law, in equity or otherwise, unless this [Agreement] expressly states that a specified remedy is the sole remedy for a specified breach.
buyside: [Company] shall not be limited to contractual remedies. All equitable, legal, statutory and contractual remedies are available for breach of this [Agreement].
sellside:
Service credits for [SLA availability failures] as specified in Schedule [SLA] are [Company]'s sole financial remedy for those specific SLA failures, provided that:
(a) the failure does not constitute an excluded liability; and
(b) [Company]'s termination, indemnity and injunctive relief rights are preserved.
fallback:
Accept "sole remedy" for service credits only where:
(a) the sole remedy applies only to specific, non-critical, narrowly-defined SLA metrics; and
(b) data breach, security incidents, regulatory breaches, wilful misconduct and Customer Asset loss are carved out.
redflags:
Broad sole remedy for all breaches — removes [Company] ability to claim damages for serious breach.
Service credits treated as full and final satisfaction of all claims arising from SLA failures, including data loss or regulatory breach.
usageNotes: Carefully review any "sole remedy" clause. Ensure it is limited to the specific metric it was negotiated for and cannot be read as limiting other remedies.

title: EQUITABLE REMEDIES AND INJUNCTIVE RELIEF
purpose: Preserves urgent non-monetary relief.
baseline:
Each Party acknowledges that a breach or threatened breach of Clause [Confidentiality], Clause [IP Ownership], Clause [Data Protection], Clause [Security], Clause [Customer Assets], or any restrictive covenant in this [Agreement] may cause immediate and irreparable harm to the affected Party for which monetary compensation would not be an adequate remedy.
Each Party is entitled, in addition to all other rights and remedies, to seek emergency, interlocutory or permanent injunctive relief, specific performance or other equitable relief from any court of competent jurisdiction, without the requirement to post a bond or prove actual damage, and without prejudice to any other remedy.
buyside:
For buy-side contracts, preserve the right to seek:
(a) mandatory orders requiring counterparty to comply with data protection, security or asset safeguarding obligations;
(b) emergency asset-freezing or preservation orders for [Customer Assets]; and
(c) urgent court orders without prior notice where immediate harm is demonstrated.
sellside: [Company] may seek injunctive relief in any jurisdiction where [Counterparty] has assets or operations, for breach of IP, data, confidentiality or acceptable use obligations.
fallback: Accept standard equitable remedies clause. Acknowledge court or tribunal may require bond in some jurisdictions.
redflags:
Injunctive relief excluded or limited to arbitration proceedings only — may be too slow for urgent IP or data breach situations.
Arbitration clause stated to be the exclusive remedy, displacing urgent court relief.
usageNotes: Dispute resolution clauses should expressly preserve the right to seek urgent court relief notwithstanding any arbitration clause.

title: SURVIVAL
purpose: Identifies obligations continuing after termination.
baseline:
The following provisions survive termination or expiry of this [Agreement] and shall continue in full force and effect:
Clause [Confidentiality], Clause [Data Protection], Clause [IP Ownership], Clause [Licence Restrictions], Clause [Payment — accrued obligations], Clause [Audit and Records], Clause [Indemnity], Clause [Limitation of Liability], Clause [Dispute Resolution], Clause [Governing Law], Clause [Consequences of Termination — data return and deletion], Clause [Customer Asset Return], Clause [Regulatory Cooperation — post-termination obligations], and Clause [Equitable Remedies].
Any other provision that by its nature is intended to survive termination shall also survive.
buyside: Include survival for all obligations that protect [Company] from post-termination harm: confidentiality (indefinitely for trade secrets), data return/deletion (until completed), audit rights (for records retained by Counterparty), regulatory cooperation, IP assignment and equitable remedies.
sellside: Ensure [Company]'s disclaimers, liability limitations, acceptable use restrictions and IP protections survive termination of [Counterparty]'s access rights.
fallback: Accept general survival language ("provisions that by their nature survive") if critical clauses are also named expressly.
redflags:
Confidentiality, data, IP, indemnity, audit or regulatory obligations do not survive termination.
Survival limited to a fixed period after which all protections extinguish.
usageNotes: Survival clause is a critical check. Review before signing to ensure all key protections are listed. Post-termination obligations on data, Customer Assets and regulatory cooperation are particularly important.

title: THIRD-PARTY RIGHTS
purpose: Controls whether non-parties can enforce contract rights.
baseline:
Except for [Company] [Affiliates] and persons expressly identified as indemnified persons in Clause [Indemnity], no person who is not a Party to this [Agreement] shall have any right to enforce any provision of this [Agreement] under any applicable law or contract principle.
This Clause does not affect any right of a third party that exists or is available other than under this [Agreement].
buyside: [Company] Affiliates, directors, officers, employees and agents shall have the right to enforce indemnity and confidentiality obligations in this [Agreement] as intended third-party beneficiaries where applicable law permits.
sellside: No third party shall have the right to enforce any provision of this [Agreement] against [Company], including [Counterparty]'s customers, end users, affiliates or sub-customers.
fallback: Accept standard no-third-party-rights clause for ordinary contracts. Third-party beneficiary rights require specific approval.
redflags:
End users, affiliates or third parties receive broad direct enforcement rights against [Company] without approval.
Third-party rights used to create customer-facing obligations on [Company] not otherwise agreed.
usageNotes: Third-party rights law varies: Singapore Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 2001; Indonesia Civil Code (limited third-party rights); Philippines Civil Code (stipulation pour autrui). Check applicable law.

title: COUNTERPARTS AND ELECTRONIC SIGNATURES
purpose: Facilitates execution while preserving evidentiary value.
baseline: This [Agreement] may be executed in one or more counterparts. Each counterpart shall constitute an original and, together, all counterparts constitute one agreement. This [Agreement] may be executed and delivered by electronic signature. Electronic signatures shall have the same legal effect as original signatures to the maximum extent permitted by [Applicable Laws].
buyside:
For material contracts, require:
(a) execution through an approved electronic signature platform (e.g. DocuSign, Adobe Sign);
(b) identity verification appropriate to the contract value; and
(c) audit trail and record of execution preserved by the platform.
sellside:
For customer-facing or platform contracts, [Company] may accept:
(a) click-to-accept execution; or
(b) electronic signature,
provided that the execution method is legally valid in the relevant jurisdiction and the contract value and risk profile support this approach.
fallback: Accept scanned or photographed wet-ink signatures for lower-risk contracts. Require electronic signature platform for contracts above [USD X] or involving regulated services, data, IP or Customer Assets.
redflags:
Counterparty challenges electronic signature validity to delay enforcement or avoid obligations.
Electronic execution used for contract types requiring wet-ink, notarisation or registration (e.g. deeds, mortgages, powers of attorney in some jurisdictions).
usageNotes:
Indonesia: Undang-Undang ITE permits electronic signatures but certain documents require wet-ink (e.g. AKTA notarial, certain regulatory filings).
Singapore: ETA permits electronic signatures generally; wet-ink may be required for certain types of documents.
India: IT Act permits electronic signatures but certain documents (e.g. wills, powers of attorney, negotiable instruments) require wet-ink.
Philippines: RA 8792 E-Commerce Act permits electronic signatures.

title: LANGUAGE
purpose: Manages Indonesia and cross-border language risk.
baseline: This [Agreement] is executed in the English language. If this [Agreement] is also executed in [Bahasa Indonesia] or any other language, the [English] language version shall prevail in the event of any inconsistency, subject to [Applicable Laws] requiring a different prevailing language.
buyside:
For contracts governed by or performed in Indonesia:
(a) consult Indonesian counsel regarding the applicability of Law No. 24/2009 on the Indonesian language requirement;
(b) prepare a bilingual (English / Bahasa Indonesia) version if required or advisable; and
(c) specify the prevailing language carefully, taking into account enforcement risk in Indonesian courts.
sellside: This [Agreement] is in English. [Counterparty] confirms it has had the opportunity to seek independent legal advice on the content of this [Agreement] in the language of its choice.
fallback: Accept translation after signing only with counsel approval confirming no execution risk and alignment of meaning in both language versions.
redflags:
No Bahasa Indonesia version where required by applicable law — creates enforcement risk.
Conflicting language versions without a clearly specified prevailing language rule.
usageNotes: Indonesia Law No. 24/2009 and its implementing regulations require Bahasa Indonesia for certain contracts involving Indonesian parties or performed in Indonesia. Verify with Indonesian counsel before relying solely on English versions.

title: GOVERNING LAW
purpose: Determines legal framework for interpretation and enforcement.
baseline: This [Agreement] and all non-contractual obligations arising out of or in connection with it shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of [specified jurisdiction], excluding its conflict-of-law rules.
sellside: [Company] prefers Singapore law for platform and technology supply agreements involving [Company Technologies Pte. Ltd.], subject to mandatory law overrides. Indonesian law applies to contracts where Indonesian entities are involved and where applicable law requires it.
fallback:
Accept counterparty's home jurisdiction law only if:
(a) enforcement, mandatory law, tax, regulatory and dispute risks have been assessed by Legal; and
(b) enforcement against [Company] in that jurisdiction is not materially disadvantageous.
redflags:
Governing law chosen without connection to parties or performance — creates enforcement risk.
Governing law creates material disadvantage for [Company] (e.g. jurisdiction hostile to [Company] interests, limited legal infrastructure, or mandatory consumer protection laws that override commercial protections).
No governing law clause — creates uncertainty.
usageNotes:
Governing law selection is a strategic decision. For cross-border contracts, Singapore law is generally preferred for its certainty, commercial sophistication and enforceability.
For Indonesian entities, Indonesian law may be mandatory for certain regulated activities. Verify with Indonesian counsel.

title: DISPUTE RESOLUTION
purpose: Provides enforceable escalation and forum.
baseline:
71.1  Escalation. If a dispute arises under this [Agreement], the Parties shall first escalate to their respective senior representatives for good-faith resolution within [30] days of written notice.
71.2  Arbitration / Court. If unresolved, disputes shall be submitted to:
Option A (Arbitration): [SIAC / BANI / ICC] arbitration in [Singapore / Jakarta / [city]], under [SIAC / BANI / ICC] Rules, with [3 / 1] arbitrator(s), conducted in [English / Bahasa Indonesia]. The arbitration award shall be final and binding.
Option B (Court): The courts of [Singapore / Indonesia / [jurisdiction]] shall have exclusive jurisdiction.
71.3  Emergency Relief. Nothing restricts either Party from seeking urgent or interim relief from any court of competent jurisdiction.
buyside:
For cross-border, high-value or regulated contracts, prefer SIAC arbitration in Singapore. For Indonesia-domestic contracts, consider BANI arbitration or Indonesian courts depending on enforcement needs. Preserve:
(a) emergency arbitrator rights (SIAC Emergency Arbitrator Procedure);
(b) urgent court interim relief notwithstanding arbitration; and
(c) debt recovery carve-outs from arbitration for clear, undisputed payment obligations.
sellside:
[Company] prefers:
(a) Singapore courts for [Company Technologies Pte. Ltd.] commercial contracts; or
(b) SIAC arbitration for cross-border, high-value or enforcement-sensitive contracts.
For customer platform terms, [Company] reserves the right to bring debt recovery and urgent injunctive proceedings in any competent court.
fallback: Accept mediation as a mandatory step before arbitration only where the mediation process does not exceed [30] days and does not restrict either Party from seeking urgent relief.
redflags:
Forum inconvenient to [Company] with no practical enforcement route.
Mandatory multi-step dispute process with no emergency relief exception.
Arbitration clause stated to be exclusive remedy, blocking urgent court orders.
Class action or collective proceedings against [Company] without Documented Approval.
usageNotes:
SIAC Rules provide for Emergency Arbitrator proceedings (within 1-2 days) for urgent interim relief.
For Indonesia, BANI is the preferred arbitration body for Indonesia-domestic arbitration. SIAC awards are enforceable in Indonesia under the New York Convention.
For Philippines and India, local enforcement proceedings for foreign arbitral awards can be lengthy. Consider carefully.

title: BOILERPLATE HIERARCHY AND CONFLICT PROVISIONS
purpose: Ensures boilerplate does not undermine core clauses.
baseline: Boilerplate provisions shall be interpreted consistently with and subject to the operative commercial, regulatory, data, security, IP, liability, indemnity and termination provisions. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between a specific provision and a general provision, the specific provision shall prevail.
buyside: Ensure DPA, information security schedule and regulatory compliance schedules prevail over general boilerplate for their subject matter.
sellside: [Company]'s acceptable use policy, platform terms and service documentation shall prevail over [Counterparty]'s general boilerplate for matters relating to platform access, usage restrictions and service parameters.
fallback: Accept standard conflict of provisions clause where order of precedence is clearly documented.
redflags: General boilerplate (e.g. limitation of liability, entire agreement) stated to prevail over specific negotiated risk provisions (e.g. DPA, security schedule, IP clause).
usageNotes: Check for conflicts between main body and schedules at final review stage. Ensure schedule precedence is clearly documented.

title: EXECUTION BLOCKS, SIGNING AUTHORITY AND APPROVALS
purpose: Ensures valid execution and internal governance compliance.
baseline:
Each signatory represents and warrants that he or she:
(a) is duly authorised to execute this [Agreement] on behalf of the relevant Party;
(b) has obtained all necessary internal approvals, board resolutions and regulatory consents required for execution; and
(c) confirms that the execution of this [Agreement] does not breach any provision of its constitutional documents or any agreement by which the relevant Party is bound.
sellside:
[Company] may accept execution through:
(a) authorised electronic signature platforms (DocuSign, Adobe Sign); or
(b) clickwrap acceptance for standard platform terms,
subject to [Company]'s internal delegation of authority requirements.
fallback: Accept standard signature blocks for ordinary contracts. Require additional evidence (board resolution, POA, witness) for high-value, regulated, M&A or financing transactions.
redflags:
Wrong legal entity signing — creates enforcement against non-intended entity.
Signatory without authority, undisclosed conflict of interest, or signing in personal capacity.
Missing company stamp / notarisation / apostille where required by applicable law.
usageNotes:
Indonesia: certain contracts require company stamp (cap perusahaan) and may require notarisation.
Philippines: certain documents require notarisation to be admissible in evidence.
India: certain contracts require stamp duty payment before enforcement.

title: SCHEDULES AND ANNEXES
purpose: Ensures schedules are legally consistent and complete.
baseline:
All Schedules, Annexes and Order Forms attached to this [Agreement] form an integral part of this [Agreement]. Each Schedule shall be consistent with the provisions of the main body. In the event of any conflict between a Schedule and the main body, the order of precedence in Clause [Order of Precedence] shall apply.
No term in a Schedule, Annex, Order Form, Statement of Work, Purchase Order or online policy shall expand, limit, override or contradict the main body of this [Agreement] unless expressly stated in the Order of Precedence clause.
sellside: For sell-side, use Order Forms for commercial terms (pricing, volume, user count) but keep all legal protections in the Master Agreement. Ensure Order Forms cannot override Master Agreement terms.
fallback: Accept Schedules containing operational details (reporting formats, delivery addresses, technical specifications) without full legal review provided they do not contain legal terms, risk allocations or obligations not covered by the main body.
redflags: Schedules contain hidden liability, exclusivity, data processing expansions, security reductions, or renewal/termination provisions not reviewed by Legal. Legal terms hidden in Order Forms, Purchase Orders, SOWs or URL-referenced policies.
usageNotes:
Every Schedule must be reviewed by Legal before signing. Business teams frequently add commercial terms to SOWs and Order Forms that create unapproved legal obligations.
